# Class: ActivityInputError

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts:11](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts#L11)

Thrown synchronously by `cmd.task` when the input does not match the activity's schema.

### stackTraceLimit

> `static` **stackTraceLimit**: `number`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured *after* the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

#### Inherited from

`Error.stackTraceLimit`

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

##### targetObject

`object`

##### constructorOpt?

`Function`

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

`Error.captureStackTrace`

***

### prepareStackTrace()

> `static` **prepareStackTrace**(`err`, `stackTraces`): `any`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:56

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / WorkflowFailure

# Class: WorkflowFailure

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/workflow.ts:77](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/workflow.ts#L77)

Fails the run. There is no `cmd.fail`: a run fails when its reducer throws, which keeps
failure out of the command vocabulary and off the happy path.

Host contract: the host catches a throw from `Workflow.reduce`, appends a `failed` event
(`cause: "app_error"`, `error` = this message) and marks the run `failed`. The state
checkpoint from before the event is kept, so the run can be rewound and forked.

## Extends

* `Error`

## Constructors

### Constructor

> **new WorkflowFailure**(`message`, `details?`): `WorkflowFailure`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/workflow.ts:82](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/workflow.ts#L82)

#### Parameters

##### message

`string`

##### details?

[`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

Anything JSON that helps explain the failure, e.g. the step id and cause.

#### Returns

`WorkflowFailure`

#### Overrides

`Error.constructor`

# Interface: Activity\<I, O>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:92](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L92)

A defined activity: the value [activity](../functions/activity.md) returns, passed to `cmd.task`, [step](../functions/step.md)
and [fanOut](../functions/fanOut.md). `I` and `O` are the inferred input and output types.

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / ActivityOptions

# Interface: ActivityOptions\<I, O>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:67](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L67)

What [activity](../functions/activity.md) needs: the two Zod schemas plus optional dispatch knobs.

## Type Parameters

### I

`I` *extends* `z.ZodType`

### O

`O` *extends* `z.ZodType`

## Properties

### input

> **input**: `I`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:69](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L69)

Schema of the task input. `cmd.task` validates against it before the command leaves the reducer.

***

### leaseMs?

> `optional` **leaseMs?**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:77](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L77)

Lease a worker holds on an attempt before it must heartbeat, in milliseconds. Default [DEFAULT_LEASE_MS](../variables/DEFAULT_LEASE_MS.md). Outside the content hash.

***

### output

> **output**: `O`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:71](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L71)

Schema of the handler's return value. The host validates against it before folding `task_done`.

***

### queue?

> `optional` **queue?**: `string`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:75](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L75)

Queue the task is dispatched on. Default [DEFAULT_QUEUE](../variables/DEFAULT_QUEUE.md). Outside the content hash.

***

### retry?

> `optional` **retry?**: [`RetryOptions`](RetryOptions.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:73](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L73)

Retry policy; see [RetryOptions](RetryOptions.md). Part of the content hash. Default [DEFAULT_RETRY](../variables/DEFAULT_RETRY.md).

***

### timeoutMs?

> `optional` **timeoutMs?**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:85](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L85)

Wall-clock budget for one attempt. The worker aborts the handler at it and reports
`cause: "timeout"`; the host reaps the attempt if the worker never answers at all.

Deliberately outside the content hash: a timeout is an operational knob, not part of the
activity's contract, so tuning it must not version the schema out from under live runs.

***

## Properties

### id?

> `optional` **id?**: `string`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts:50](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts#L50)

Step id of the wait. Defaults to a kernel-derived id.

***

### timeoutMs?

> `optional` **timeoutMs?**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts:56](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts#L56)

Deadline for the wait, counted from the timestamp of the event being reduced. A `timer`
event with step id `<id>:timeout` reaches the reducer when the deadline passes; the
losing side of the race is cancelled by the kernel. Requires an explicit `id`.

Step id of the task.

###### ts_ms

`number`

Journaled event time, epoch milliseconds.

###### type

`"task_done"`

A task reached a terminal status.

###### usage

[`Usage`](Usage.md)

What this attempt itself consumed; zeroed when the worker reported none.

###### usage_total

[`Usage`](Usage.md)

The run's banked usage including this event.

#### Returns

[`Reduction`](../type-aliases/Reduction.md)<`S`>

***

# Interface: QueueProfile

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/config/define.ts:56](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/config/define.ts#L56)

How tasks on one queue reach their workers. A queue with neither `url` nor `mode` is
served only by a worker in the same process.

## Properties

### mode?

> `optional` **mode?**: `"push"` | `"pull"`

`"push"` delivers to `url`; `"pull"` never pushes and lets workers long-poll the host instead.

***

### secret?

***

# Interface: RetryOptions

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:39](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L39)

Authoring form of [RetryPolicy](RetryPolicy.md) (camelCase, all optional); the wire form is
snake_case. Every omitted field falls back to [DEFAULT_RETRY](../variables/DEFAULT_RETRY.md).

## Properties

### backoff?

> `optional` **backoff?**: [`Backoff`](../type-aliases/Backoff.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:43](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L43)

`"fixed"` waits `initialMs` every time; `"exponential"` multiplies it by `factor` per attempt. Default `"exponential"`.

***

### factor?

> `optional` **factor?**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:49](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L49)

Growth multiplier for exponential backoff; a value ≤ 1 behaves like fixed. Default `2`.

***

### initialMs?

> `optional` **initialMs?**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:45](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L45)

Delay before the second attempt, in milliseconds. Default `1_000`.

***

### jitter?

> `optional` **jitter?**: [`Jitter`](../type-aliases/Jitter.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:51](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L51)

`"full"` scales each delay by a journaled random fraction; `"none"` uses it as is. Default `"full"`.

***

### maxAttempts?

> `optional` **maxAttempts?**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:41](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L41)

Attempts in total, the first one included. Default `3`.

***

### maxMs?

> `optional` **maxMs?**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:47](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L47)

Ceiling on any single delay, in milliseconds. Default `600_000`.

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / RetryPolicy

# Interface: RetryPolicy

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:116](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L116)

Wire form of a retry policy; the authoring form is `RetryOptions`. The delay before
attempt `n + 1` is `initial_ms` (fixed) or `initial_ms · factor^(n − 1)` (exponential),
capped at `max_ms`, then jittered. Retrying stops at `max_attempts` or on a cause that
never retries.

## Properties

### backoff

> **backoff**: [`Backoff`](../type-aliases/Backoff.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:120](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L120)

Delay growth strategy.

***

### factor

> **factor**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:126](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L126)

Growth multiplier for exponential backoff; ≤ 1 behaves like fixed.

***

### initial_ms

> **initial_ms**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:122](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L122)

Delay before the second attempt, in milliseconds.

***

### jitter

> **jitter**: [`Jitter`](../type-aliases/Jitter.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:128](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L128)

Jitter applied to every delay.

***

### max_attempts

> **max_attempts**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:118](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L118)

Attempts in total, the first one included.

***

### max_ms

> **max_ms**: `number`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:124](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L124)

Ceiling on any single delay, in milliseconds.

### reportUsage()

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts:34](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts#L34)

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / ActivityHandler

# Type Alias: ActivityHandler\<I, O>

> **ActivityHandler**<`I`, `O`> = (`input`, `ctx`) => `O` | `Promise`<`O`>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts:45](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts#L45)

The implementation of one activity. `input` has already passed the activity's input
schema; the return value is validated against its output schema by the host. A throw
fails the attempt as retryable; aborting on `ctx.signal` is how a handler cooperates
with a timeout, a lost lease or a shutdown.

## Type Parameters

### I

`I` = [`Json`](Json.md)

### O

`O` = `unknown`

## Parameters

### input

`I`

### ctx

[`TaskContext`](../interfaces/TaskContext.md)

## Returns

`O` | `Promise`<`O`>

Handler inputs are contravariant, so `never` accepts any concretely typed handler.

# Type Alias: Backoff

> **Backoff** = `"fixed"` | `"exponential"`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:106](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L106)

`fixed` repeats `initial_ms`; `exponential` multiplies it by `factor` per attempt.

url: /vlo/api/index/type-aliases/Cause.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / Cause

# Type Alias: Cause

> **Cause** = `"timeout"` | `"heartbeat_lost"` | `"app_error"` | `"user_cancel"` | `"schema_violation"` | `"nondeterminism_detected"`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:41](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L41)

Why a step or run failed. `timeout`: the attempt ran past `timeout_ms`; `heartbeat_lost`:
the lease expired; `app_error`: the handler or reducer threw; `user_cancel`: cancelled
through the API; `schema_violation`: a worker's output failed the output schema;
`nondeterminism_detected`: a re-fold diverged from the journal. The last three never retry.

The terminal status a child run reports to its parent, mapped from the child's run status.

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / Command

# Type Alias: Command

> **Command** = { `activity`: `string`; `id?`: `string`; `input`: [`Json`](Json.md); `lease_ttl_ms?`: `number`; `queue?`: `string`; `retry?`: [`RetryPolicy`](../interfaces/RetryPolicy.md); `schema_ref?`: `string`; `timeout_ms?`: `number`; `type`: `"task"`; } | { `fire_at_ms?`: `number`; `fire_in_ms?`: `number`; `id?`: `string`; `type`: `"timer"`; } | { `id?`: `string`; `input`: [`Json`](Json.md); `type`: `"spawn"`; `workflow`: `string`; } | { `id?`: `string`; `name`: `string`; `schema_ref?`: `string`; `timeout_ms?`: `number`; `type`: `"await_signal"`; } | { `channel`: `string`; `data`: [`Json`](Json.md); `type`: `"emit"`; } | { `output`: [`Json`](Json.md); `type`: `"complete"`; } | { `input`: [`Json`](Json.md); `type`: `"continue_as_new"`; }

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:136](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L136)

A command as a reducer returns it and the kernel validates it. Build them with `cmd.*`.
`task`, `timer`, `spawn` and `await_signal` open a step and take an optional step `id`
(default: kernel-derived, `${type}#${step_no}`); `complete` and `continue_as_new` must be last.

## Union Members

### Type Literal

{ `activity`: `string`; `id?`: `string`; `input`: [`Json`](Json.md); `lease_ttl_ms?`: `number`; `queue?`: `string`; `retry?`: [`RetryPolicy`](../interfaces/RetryPolicy.md); `schema_ref?`: `string`; `timeout_ms?`: `number`; `type`: `"task"`; }

#### activity

> **activity**: `string`

Activity name.

#### id?

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / Status

# Type Alias: Status

> **Status** = `"scheduled"` | `"running"` | `"succeeded"` | `"failed"` | `"retrying"` | `"cancelled"` | `"awaiting_signal"`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts:26](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/protocol.ts#L26)

Status of one step (a task, timer, signal wait or child), as carried on every event.
`scheduled` → `running` → `succeeded` | `failed` | `retrying` | `cancelled`;
`awaiting_signal` is a parked wait. `succeeded`, `failed` and `cancelled` are terminal.

url: /vlo/api/index/variables/cmd.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / cmd

# Variable: cmd

> `const` **cmd**: `object`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts:236](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/commands.ts#L236)

The command constructors a reducer returns to the engine. Each builds a plain
[Command](../type-aliases/Command.md); nothing runs until the host applies the reduction. `task`, `timer`,
`spawn` and `awaitSignal` open a step, `emit` records a side effect, `complete` and
`continueAsNew` close the run and must come last.

## Type Declaration

### awaitHuman

> **awaitHuman**: <`T`>(`definition`, `options`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)\[]

`awaitSignal` with a deadline + `emit("human", …)`; returns a `Command[]`.

Ask a human. Sugar over `await_signal` (with its deadline) + `emit`: the wait reserves
`id` and the kernel opens `${id}:timeout` beside it, so whichever arrives first wins and
the kernel cancels the loser. Returns commands — spread it into a reduction.

#### Type Parameters

##### T

`T`

#### Parameters

##### definition

[`SignalDef`](../interfaces/SignalDef.md)<`T`>

##### options

[`AwaitHumanOptions`](../interfaces/AwaitHumanOptions.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)\[]

### awaitSignal

> **awaitSignal**: <`T`>(`definition`, `options?`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

Parks the run until the named signal is delivered.

Parks the run until a signal named after `definition` is delivered; the payload arrives
on a `signal` event. A signal that arrived before the wait was opened is buffered and
delivered immediately, oldest first. The run holds no compute while parked. With
`timeoutMs` the kernel also opens a timer step `<id>:timeout` and cancels whichever of
the two loses; see [signalTimeoutStepId](../functions/signalTimeoutStepId.md).

#### Type Parameters

##### T

`T`

#### Parameters

##### definition

[`SignalDef`](../interfaces/SignalDef.md)<`T`>

##### options?

[`AwaitSignalOptions`](../interfaces/AwaitSignalOptions.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

### complete

> **complete**: (`output`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

Closes the run as `completed`. Must be last.

Closes the run as `completed` with `output`. It must be the last command of the reduction;
the kernel rejects any command after it.

#### Parameters

##### output

[`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

### continueAsNew

> **continueAsNew**: (`input`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

Closes the run as `continued` with a fresh start input. Must be last.

Closes the run as `continued`, carrying `input` as the start input of a successor run. It
must be the last command of the reduction. The host starts the successor (same workflow,
this `input`) in the same transaction and links the two runs by `continued_from` and
`continued_to`; a parent run is notified once, by the run that finally closes.

#### Parameters

##### input

[`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

### emit

> **emit**: (`channel`, `data`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

Publishes on a side channel; never journaled.

Publishes `data` on a side channel. Emits never enter the run's history and never come
back to the reducer; the host forwards them to event-stream subscribers, which is where
progress ticks and UI hints belong.

#### Parameters

##### channel

`string`

##### data

[`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

### spawn

> **spawn**: (`workflow`, `input`, `options?`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

Starts a child run; its result arrives as `child_done`.

Starts a child run of `workflow` (a name, or anything with a `name` such as a
[Workflow](../interfaces/Workflow.md)) with `input`. The child's terminal status and output come back to this
run as a `child_done` event on the spawn's step id. The workflow must be registered on
the host that dispatches the command.

#### Parameters

##### workflow

`string` | { `name`: `string`; }

##### input

[`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

##### options?

[`SpawnOptions`](../interfaces/SpawnOptions.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

### task

> **task**: <`I`, `O`>(`target`, `input`, `options?`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

Runs an activity once, with retries. Throws [ActivityInputError](../classes/ActivityInputError.md) on bad input.

Requests one attempt-tracked execution of `target` with `input`.

`input` is parsed with the activity's Zod schema; the parsed value (defaults applied) is
what travels. The activity's `queue`, `retry`, `leaseMs` and `timeoutMs` are copied onto
the command; `options.queue` overrides the queue for this call.

#### Type Parameters

##### I

`I`

##### O

`O`

#### Parameters

##### target

[`Activity`](../interfaces/Activity.md)<`I`, `O`>

##### input

`I`

##### options?

[`TaskOptions`](../interfaces/TaskOptions.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

#### Throws

[ActivityInputError](../classes/ActivityInputError.md) when the input does not match the activity's schema.

### timer

> **timer**: (`options`) => [`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

Fires a `timer` event after `ms` or at `atMs`.

Schedules a `timer` event for the run. `ms` is relative to the timestamp of the event
being reduced; `atMs` is absolute epoch milliseconds.

Throws a `TypeError` synchronously when neither or both of `ms` / `atMs` are given.

#### Parameters

##### options

[`TimerOptions`](../interfaces/TimerOptions.md)

#### Returns

[`Command`](../type-aliases/Command.md)

## Example

```ts
import { cmd, defineWorkflow } from "@oona/vlo";
import { approve, work } from "./activities.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("review", {
  init: (input: { item: string }) => ({ item: input.item, upper: null as string | null }),
  on: {
    started: (s) => [s, [cmd.task(work, { item: s.item })]],
    task_done: (s, e) => [
      { ...s, upper: (e.output as { upper: string }).upper },
      cmd.awaitHuman(approve, { id: "approval", timeoutMs: 86_400_000 }),
    ],
    signal: (s) => [s, [cmd.complete({ upper: s.upper })]],
    timer: (s) => [s, [cmd.complete(null)]],
  },
});
```

# Variable: DEFAULT_RETRY

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / activity

# Function: activity()

> **activity**<`I`, `O`>(`name`, `options`): [`Activity`](../interfaces/Activity.md)<`output`<`I`>, `output`<`O`>>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:160](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L160)

Defines an activity: a named unit of work a worker implements and a reducer requests
with `cmd.task`.

The content hash covers `name`, both schemas (as JSON Schema, projected by
[projectSchema](projectSchema.md) so annotations such as `description` and `default` are
hash-neutral) and the resolved retry policy, so changing any of them yields a new
`schemaRef`; `queue`, `leaseMs` and `timeoutMs` are operational and hash-neutral. Runs
pin the `schemaRef` per event, so old and new versions coexist.

## Type Parameters

### I

`I` *extends* `ZodType`<`unknown`, `unknown`, `$ZodTypeInternals`<`unknown`, `unknown`>>

### O

`O` *extends* `ZodType`<`unknown`, `unknown`, `$ZodTypeInternals`<`unknown`, `unknown`>>

## Parameters

### name

`string`

### options

[`ActivityOptions`](../interfaces/ActivityOptions.md)<`I`, `O`>

## Returns

[`Activity`](../interfaces/Activity.md)<`output`<`I`>, `output`<`O`>>

## Example

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { activity } from "@oona/vlo";

export const work = activity("example.work", {
  input: z.object({ item: z.string() }),
  output: z.object({ upper: z.string() }),
  retry: { maxAttempts: 3 },
  queue: "default",
  timeoutMs: 30_000,
});
```

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / canonicalJson

# Function: canonicalJson()

> **canonicalJson**(`value`): `string`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/hash.ts:22](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/hash.ts#L22)

Deterministic JSON: object keys sorted recursively, arrays in order, no whitespace.
Throws on anything JSON cannot represent losslessly (undefined, NaN, Infinity, bigint,
function, symbol) rather than silently dropping it, because a dropped field would make
two different schemas hash the same.

## Parameters

### value

`unknown`

## Returns

`string`

# Function: defineWorker()

> **defineWorker**(`impls`, `options?`): [`Worker`](../interfaces/Worker.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts:96](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts#L96)

Defines a worker: a map from activity name to [ActivityHandler](../type-aliases/ActivityHandler.md) plus the queues it
serves. Passed to `createHost({ workers })` for in-process execution, `runPullWorker` for
long-polling, or found by the config loader's `workers` globs.

The worker holds no schemas; validation happens in the reducer (input) and on the host
(output). Throws a `TypeError` when `impls` is empty.

## Parameters

### impls

[`ActivityImpls`](../type-aliases/ActivityImpls.md)

### options?

[`WorkerOptions`](../interfaces/WorkerOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

[`Worker`](../interfaces/Worker.md)

## Example

```ts
import { defineWorker } from "@oona/vlo";

export default defineWorker(
  {
    "example.plan": (input: { n: number }) => ({
      items: Array.from({ length: input.n }, (_, i) => `item-${i}`),
    }),
    "example.work": async (input: { item: string }, ctx) => {
      await ctx.heartbeat();
      ctx.reportUsage({ tokens: 12 });
      return { upper: input.item.toUpperCase() };
    },
  },
  { queues: ["default"] },
);
```

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / defineWorkflow

# Function: defineWorkflow()

> **defineWorkflow**<`S`, `I`>(`name`, `def`): [`Workflow`](../interfaces/Workflow.md)<`S`, `I`>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/workflow.ts:112](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/workflow.ts#L112)

Defines a workflow: a named, pure reducer over the run's events.

`def` is either a hand-written [WorkflowDef](../interfaces/WorkflowDef.md) or the output of [sequence](sequence.md).
Handlers must not read a clock, generate randomness or do I/O; time and randomness arrive
on the event. State must be JSON-serialisable: it is stringified after every reduction.
A handler that throws fails the run (see [WorkflowFailure](../classes/WorkflowFailure.md)); so does an event
whose handler is not registered, or a handler returning anything but `[state, Command[]]`.

## Type Parameters

### S

`S`

### I

`I`

## Parameters

### name

`string`

### def

[`WorkflowDef`](../interfaces/WorkflowDef.md)<`S`, `I`>

## Returns

[`Workflow`](../interfaces/Workflow.md)<`S`, `I`>

## Example

```ts
import { cmd, defineWorkflow } from "@oona/vlo";
import { work } from "./activities.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("uppercase", {
  init: (input: { item: string }) => ({ item: input.item }),
  on: {
    started: (s) => [s, [cmd.task(work, { item: s.item })]],
    task_done: (s, e) => [s, [cmd.complete(e.output ?? null)]],
  },
});
```

# Function: env()

> **env**(`name`, `options?`): [`EnvRef`](../interfaces/EnvRef.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/config/define.ts:43](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/config/define.ts#L43)

Refers to an environment variable by name so a secret never sits in `vlo.config.ts`.

The value is read when the profile is loaded, not when `env` is called. An unset or empty
variable fails the load with a message naming the variable, unless `optional` is `true`,
in which case the field is simply absent.

## Parameters

### options?

`boolean`

## Example

```ts
import { defineConfig, env } from "@oona/vlo";

export default defineConfig({
  workflows: ["*.workflow.ts"],
  profiles: {
    prod: {
      journal: env("DATABASE_URL"),
      auth: { token: env("VLO_TOKEN"), pushSecret: env("VLO_PUSH_SECRET", { optional: true }) },

  },
});
```

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / fanOut

# Function: fanOut()

> **fanOut**<`I`, `O`>(`target`, `select`, `options`): [`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts:113](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts#L113)

A [sequence](sequence.md) phase that runs `target` once per item `select` returns, at most
`concurrency` at a time, with step ids `${target.name}#${index}`.

`select` must be pure and read only state written by earlier phases: it is re-evaluated
on every event of the phase and the run fails if it returns a different count. Outputs
are stored in `results[target.name]` in item order; an empty selection stores `[]` and
moves on. A task that does not succeed fails the run, unless `onFailure: "continue"`
stores `null` for that item.

Throws a `TypeError` synchronously unless `concurrency` is an integer ≥ 1.

## Type Parameters

### I

`I`

### O

`O`

## Parameters

### target

[`Activity`](../interfaces/Activity.md)<`I`, `O`>

### select

(`state`) => `I`\[]

### options

[`FanOutOptions`](../interfaces/FanOutOptions.md)

## Returns

[`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

## Example

```ts
import { defineWorkflow, fanOut, resultOf, sequence, step } from "@oona/vlo";
import { plan, work } from "./activities.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("example", sequence([
  step(plan),
  fanOut(work, (state) => resultOf(state, plan).items.map((item) => ({ item })), { concurrency: 2 }),
]));
```

# Function: fanOutResultsOf()

> **fanOutResultsOf**<`I`, `O`>(`state`, `target`): `O`\[]

The outputs of an earlier [fanOut](fanOut.md) on `target`, in item order. An empty

---
url: /vlo/api/index/functions/fanOutRuns.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / fanOutRuns

# Function: fanOutRuns()

> **fanOutRuns**<`I`>(`target`, `select`, `options`): [`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts:157](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts#L157)

A [sequence](sequence.md) phase that spawns one child run of `target` per item `select` returns,
at most `concurrency` at a time, with step ids `${workflow}#${index}`.

`select` has the same purity rule as [fanOut](fanOut.md). Each item is the child's start input.
The phase stores a [ChildResult](../interfaces/ChildResult.md) per item in `results[workflow]`, in item order;
read it with [fanOutRunsResultsOf](fanOutRunsResultsOf.md). An empty selection stores `[]` and moves on.
A child that did not complete fails the run, unless `onFailure: "continue"` records its
status and moves on. The child workflow must be registered on the same host.

Throws a `TypeError` synchronously unless `concurrency` is an integer ≥ 1.

## Type Parameters

### I

`I` *extends* [`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md) = [`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

## Parameters

### target

`string` | { `name`: `string`; }

### select

(`state`) => `I`\[]

### options

[`FanOutRunsOptions`](../interfaces/FanOutRunsOptions.md)

## Returns

[`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

## Example

```ts
import { defineWorkflow, fanOutRuns, fanOutRunsResultsOf, resultOf, sequence, step } from "@oona/vlo";
import { plan, summarise } from "./activities.ts";
import { readSource } from "./read-source.workflow.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("research", sequence([
  step(plan),
  fanOutRuns(readSource, (s) => resultOf(s, plan).sourceIds.map((sourceId) => ({ sourceId })), {
    concurrency: 5,
    onFailure: "continue",
  }),
  step(summarise, (s) => ({ read: fanOutRunsResultsOf(s, readSource).filter((r) => r.status === "succeeded").length })),
]));
```

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / fanOutRunsResultsOf

# Function: fanOutRunsResultsOf()

> **fanOutRunsResultsOf**<`O`>(`state`, `target`): [`ChildResult`](../interfaces/ChildResult.md)<`O`>\[]

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence-access.ts:55](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence-access.ts#L55)

The outcomes of an earlier [fanOutRuns](fanOutRuns.md) on `target`, in item order: one
[ChildResult](../interfaces/ChildResult.md) per child, whose `output` is `null` unless the child completed. An
empty selection stored `[]`. `O` is the child workflow's completion output type.

## Type Parameters

### O

`O` = [`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

## Parameters

### state

[`SeqState`](../interfaces/SeqState.md)

### target

`string` | { `name`: `string`; }

## Returns

[`ChildResult`](../interfaces/ChildResult.md)<`O`>\[]

## Example

```ts
step(summarise, (state) => ({
  read: fanOutRunsResultsOf<{ ok: boolean }>(state, readSource).filter((r) => r.output?.ok).length,
}))
```

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / projectSchema

# Function: projectSchema()

> **projectSchema**(`schema`): [`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/schema-projection.ts:55](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/schema-projection.ts#L55)

Returns a copy of `schema` with every annotation keyword removed from every schema
object in it. Arrays are walked (`anyOf`, `prefixItems`, …) in order; the entries of a
name-keyed map (`properties`, `$defs`, …) keep their names and have their values
projected; scalars pass through. The input is never mutated.

## Parameters

### schema

[`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

## Returns

[`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)

url: /vlo/api/index/functions/sequence.md

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / sequence

# Function: sequence()

> **sequence**(`steps`, `options?`): [`WorkflowDef`](../interfaces/WorkflowDef.md)<[`SeqState`](../interfaces/SeqState.md), [`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts:254](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts#L254)

Compiles an ordered list of phases into a [WorkflowDef](../interfaces/WorkflowDef.md) for [defineWorkflow](defineWorkflow.md).

Phases run one after another: [step](step.md), [fanOut](fanOut.md), [fanOutRuns](fanOutRuns.md),
[waitFor](waitFor.md) and [sleep](sleep.md). Outputs go to `results` keyed by activity or workflow
name and signal payloads to `signals` keyed by signal name, so two phases on the same
target share a key. After the last phase the run completes with `results`, or with
`options.output(state)`. `state.usage` always holds the run's banked usage as of the
last event. Events that do not belong to the current phase are ignored: state
unchanged, no commands.

## Parameters

### steps

readonly [`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)\[]

### options?

[`SequenceOptions`](../interfaces/SequenceOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

[`WorkflowDef`](../interfaces/WorkflowDef.md)<[`SeqState`](../interfaces/SeqState.md), [`Json`](../type-aliases/Json.md)>

## Example

```ts
import {
  defineWorkflow, fanOut, fanOutResultsOf, resultOf, sequence, signalOf, step, waitFor,
} from "@oona/vlo";
import { approve, finish, plan, work } from "./activities.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("example", sequence([
  step(plan),
  fanOut(work, (s) => resultOf(s, plan).items.map((item) => ({ item })), { concurrency: 2 }),
  waitFor(approve),
  step(finish, (s) => ({
    uppers: fanOutResultsOf(s, work).map((o) => o.upper),
    approvedBy: signalOf(s, approve).by,
  })),
], { output: (s) => ({ report: resultOf(s, finish).report, tokens: s.usage?.tokens ?? 0 }) }));
```

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / signal

# Function: signal()

> **signal**<`S`>(`name`, `schema`): [`SignalDef`](../interfaces/SignalDef.md)<`output`<`S`>>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts:210](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/activity.ts#L210)

Defines a signal: a named, typed message a run can park on with `cmd.awaitSignal`,
`cmd.awaitHuman` or [waitFor](waitFor.md), delivered from outside through the host's API.

The content hash covers `name` and the schema as JSON Schema, projected the same way as
an activity's. A host that has the definition registered rejects an inbound payload the
schema does not accept.

## Type Parameters

### S

`S` *extends* `ZodType`<`unknown`, `unknown`, `$ZodTypeInternals`<`unknown`, `unknown`>>

## Parameters

### name

`string`

### schema

`S`

## Returns

[`SignalDef`](../interfaces/SignalDef.md)<`output`<`S`>>

## Example

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { signal } from "@oona/vlo";

export const approve = signal("example.approve", z.object({ by: z.string() }));
```

# Function: signalOf()

> **signalOf**<`T`>(`state`, `definition`): `T`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence-access.ts:73](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence-access.ts#L73)

The payload an earlier [waitFor](waitFor.md) on `definition` received, typed as the signal's
payload. After an `onTimeout: "continue"` deadline the stored value is `null`, which
this returns as-is; narrow it yourself when that option is in play.

## Type Parameters

### T

`T`

## Parameters

### state

[`SeqState`](../interfaces/SeqState.md)

### definition

[`SignalDef`](../interfaces/SignalDef.md)<`T`>

## Returns

`T`

## Example

```ts
step(finish, (state) => ({ uppers: [], approvedBy: signalOf(state, approve).by }))
```

# Function: sleep()

> **sleep**(`ms`): [`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts:221](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts#L221)

A [sequence](sequence.md) phase that parks the run on a timer for `ms` milliseconds. It stores
nothing: the phase after it receives the value of the last phase that stored one.

## Parameters

### ms

`number`

## Returns

[`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

## Example

```ts
import { defineWorkflow, sequence, sleep, step } from "@oona/vlo";
import { plan, finish } from "./activities.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("example", sequence([
  step(plan),
  sleep(60_000),
  step(finish, (state) => ({ uppers: [], approvedBy: "timer" })),
]));
```

url: /vlo/api/index/functions/step.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / step

# Function: step()

> **step**<`I`, `O`>(`target`, `mapInput?`, `options?`): [`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts:72](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts#L72)

A [sequence](sequence.md) phase that runs `target` once.

Without `mapInput` the task input is the run's start input for phase 0 and the previous
phase's stored value afterwards (sleeps are skipped). The output is stored in
`results[target.name]`. A task that does not succeed fails the run, unless
`onFailure: "continue"` stores `null` instead; `when` returning `false` also stores `null`
and skips the task. `id` pins the step id for handlers that key on it.

## Type Parameters

### I

`I`

### O

`O`

## Parameters

### target

[`Activity`](../interfaces/Activity.md)<`I`, `O`>

### mapInput?

(`state`) => `I`

### options?

[`StepOptions`](../interfaces/StepOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

[`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

## Example

```ts
import { defineWorkflow, resultOf, sequence, step } from "@oona/vlo";
import { finish, notify, plan } from "./activities.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("example", sequence([
  step(plan),
  step(finish, (state) => ({ uppers: resultOf(state, plan).items, approvedBy: "auto" })),
  step(notify, undefined, { onFailure: "continue", when: (s) => resultOf(s, plan).items.length > 0 }),
]));
```

---

---
url: /vlo/api/index/functions/waitFor.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / waitFor

# Function: waitFor()

> **waitFor**<`T`>(`definition`, `options?`): [`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts:194](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/core/helpers/sequence.ts#L194)

A [sequence](sequence.md) phase that parks the run until `definition` is delivered.

The payload is stored in `signals[definition.name]`. With `timeoutMs` the wait races the
kernel's paired deadline timer (the loser is cancelled): `onTimeout: "fail"` (default)
fails the run, `"continue"` stores `null` and advances. `context` is emitted on the
`human` channel when the wait opens. A signal or deadline arriving for a phase already
left behind is ignored.

## Type Parameters

### T

`T`

## Parameters

### definition

[`SignalDef`](../interfaces/SignalDef.md)<`T`>

### options?

[`WaitForOptions`](../interfaces/WaitForOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

[`SeqStep`](../type-aliases/SeqStep.md)

## Example

```ts
import { defineWorkflow, sequence, signalOf, step, waitFor } from "@oona/vlo";
import { approve, finish, plan } from "./activities.ts";

export default defineWorkflow("example", sequence([
  step(plan),
  waitFor(approve, { timeoutMs: 86_400_000, onTimeout: "fail", context: { what: "plan" } }),
  step(finish, (state) => ({ uppers: [], approvedBy: signalOf(state, approve).by })),
]));
```

---
url: /vlo/api/index/functions/withRetryInput.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [index](../index.md) / withRetryInput

# Function: withRetryInput()

> **withRetryInput**<`I`, `O`>(`handler`, `shape`): [`ActivityHandler`](../type-aliases/ActivityHandler.md)<`I`, `O`>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts:126](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/registry.ts#L126)

Wraps a handler so attempts after the first receive `shape(input, attempt)` instead of the
journaled input. Use it when repeating the same ask would fail the same way — a model
looping on a long prompt, say — and a smaller or different ask has a chance.

The journaled task input is untouched; only this process's view of it changes, and
`attempt` is journaled, so the same attempt always sees the same input. `shape` must be
pure. The shaped input is not re-validated against the activity's input schema.

## Type Parameters

### I

`I`

### O

`O`

## Parameters

### handler

[`ActivityHandler`](../type-aliases/ActivityHandler.md)<`I`, `O`>

### shape

(`input`, `attempt`) => `I`

## Returns

[`ActivityHandler`](../type-aliases/ActivityHandler.md)<`I`, `O`>

## Example

```ts
defineWorker({
  "brand.synthesize": withRetryInput(synthesize, (input) => ({ ...input, compact: true })),
});
```

### stackTraceLimit

> `static` **stackTraceLimit**: `number`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured *after* the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

#### Inherited from

[`VloError`](VloError.md).[`stackTraceLimit`](VloError.md#stacktracelimit)

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

##### targetObject

`object`

##### constructorOpt?

`Function`

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

[`VloError`](VloError.md).[`captureStackTrace`](VloError.md#capturestacktrace)

***

### prepareStackTrace()

> `static` **prepareStackTrace**(`err`, `stackTraces`): `any`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:56

# Class: InProcessTracker

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts:17](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts#L17)

Counts handlers this process still owes a result for. One tracker is shared by every
in-process transport a host builds, because `Host.drain` has to tell "the dispatcher
moved nothing" apart from "the dispatcher moved nothing *yet*: a handler is running and
its result will schedule the next task".

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / JournalClosed

# Class: JournalClosed

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/journal/types.ts:324](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/journal/types.ts#L324)

Thrown by every journal call made after `close()`.

Shutdown is inherently racy: a worker reporting a result, a stage finishing its pass. The
contract is that those calls fail with this, one recognisable error, instead of whatever
the driver does to a closed handle — `node:sqlite` raises `ERR_INVALID_STATE` from a
finalized statement, which surfaces as a crash rather than as "the host is stopping".

## Extends

* `Error`

## Constructors

### Constructor

> **new JournalClosed**(`dialect`): `JournalClosed`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/journal/types.ts:329](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/journal/types.ts#L329)

`dialect` names the implementation, e.g. `sqlite` or `postgres`.

#### Parameters

##### dialect

`string`

#### Returns

`JournalClosed`

#### Overrides

`Error.constructor`

***

### stackTraceLimit

> `static` **stackTraceLimit**: `number`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured *after* the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

#### Inherited from

`Error.stackTraceLimit`

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

##### targetObject

`object`

##### constructorOpt?

`Function`

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

`Error.captureStackTrace`

***

### prepareStackTrace()

> `static` **prepareStackTrace**(`err`, `stackTraces`): `any`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:56

#### Parameters

`Error`

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / Nondeterminism

# Class: Nondeterminism

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/errors.ts:71](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/errors.ts#L71)

The checkpoint or the re-fold disagreed with the journal. The run is failed first: the
`nondeterminism` marker it records carries `cause: "nondeterminism_detected"`, which is the
kernel's `Cause` value and stays as it is. This error's own code is `refold_mismatch`.

## Extends

`refold_mismatch`, 409.

`string`

The run that diverged.

The first journal seq the replay disagreed at; 0 when the journal holds nothing foldable.

`string`

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / ReducerFailed

# Class: ReducerFailed

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/errors.ts:90](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/errors.ts#L90)

The reducer threw, or the host could not honour what it asked for. `applyEvent` swallows
this and records a `fail` marker with `cause: "app_error"` (the kernel's `Cause` value; this
error's own code is `reducer_failed`). Also raised when a `spawn` or `continue_as_new`
names a workflow this host has not registered.

## Extends

* [`VloError`](VloError.md)

## Constructors

### Constructor

> **new ReducerFailed**(`runId`, `message`, `trigger?`, `reason?`): `ReducerFailed`

`reducer_failed`, 409. Callers of `applyEvent` never see it; the run is failed instead.

#### Parameters

##### runId

`string`

The run whose reducer threw.

##### message

`string`

##### trigger?

[`EventInput`](../interfaces/EventInput.md)

The event being folded when the reducer threw; journaled on the `fail` marker.

##### reason?

`string`

Default: `message`.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

### captureStackTrace()

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.


The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation

```js

}

}

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
```

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured *after* the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

# Class: VloError

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/errors.ts:12](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/errors.ts#L12)

Base of every error the host maps to an HTTP response. The router turns one into

***

### stackTraceLimit

> `static` **stackTraceLimit**: `number`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:68

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured *after* the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

#### Inherited from

`Error.stackTraceLimit`

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Defined in: node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@24.19.4/node_modules/@types/node/globals.d.ts:52

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js

  throw error;
```

# Interface: ActivityRegistration

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/context.ts:39](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/context.ts#L39)

An activity as the host knows it: a name and a validator for the worker's output.
`hash` and `jsonSchema` are present on real `Activity` values and drive registry
upserts on boot; a bare `{ name, output }` still validates.

# Interface: Client

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/client/index.ts:101](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/client/index.ts#L101)

The control-plane client. Every method maps to one `/v1` route and throws a plain `Error`

### startFresh()

> **startFresh**(`workflow`, `input`, `options`): `Promise`<[`StartFreshResult`](StartFreshResult.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/client/index.ts:122](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/client/index.ts#L122)

Starts a run under `runId`, or under `${runId}_2`, `_3`, … once earlier runs with the
key have ended: the first id with no run is started, a live one is joined. The walk is
deterministic, so two concurrent callers land on the same id and the insert's
`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` makes one of them the joiner.

#### Parameters

##### workflow

`string` | { `name`: `string`; }

##### input

[`Json`](../../index/type-aliases/Json.md)

##### options

[`StartFreshOptions`](StartFreshOptions.md)

#### Returns

`Promise`<[`StartFreshResult`](StartFreshResult.md)>

> **drain**(`options?`): `Promise`<[`DrainResult`](DrainResult.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts:109](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts#L109)

Ticks until the outbox is idle or `maxMs` (default 25 s) runs out. Concurrent callers
share one drain. Rejects on a host without the `orchestrator` role.

#### Returns

`Promise`<`void`>

### stop()

> **stop**(): `Promise`<`void`>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts:102](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts#L102)

Stops the dispatcher, waits up to [SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS](../variables/SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS.md) for in-process handlers, then
closes the journal if the host opened it from a URL. Idempotent.

#### Returns

`Promise`<`void`>

# Interface: InProcessOptions

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts:54](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts#L54)

Knobs for [InProcessTransport](../classes/InProcessTransport.md).

## Properties

### onError?

> `optional` **onError?**: (`error`) => `void`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts:62](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts#L62)

Where a failure to *report* goes. The handler's own throw is a task failure and the
reporter turns it into one; this is the reporter itself failing — a journal that closed
under a shutdown, typically — and without a home it would be an unhandled rejection.

#### Parameters

##### error

`unknown`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### tracker?

> `optional` **tracker?**: [`InProcessTracker`](../classes/InProcessTracker.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts:56](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transport/in-process.ts#L56)

Shared with the host, so `Host.drain` can wait for handlers this transport started.

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / SignalRunResult

# Interface: SignalRunResult

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/runs.ts:95](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/runs.ts#L95)

What [signalRun](../functions/signalRun.md) returns.

## Properties

### delivered

> **delivered**: `boolean`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/runs.ts:105](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/runs.ts#L105)

True when an open wait folded the signal into the run. False in two cases: nothing was
waiting, so the signal is buffered until a wait with that name opens; or the wait it
matched had already closed — its timeout fired first, or the run has ended — a late
signal. A late signal is recorded against the closed step, never folded, never buffered,
and the stale wait row is dropped.

***

### signal_id

> **signal_id**: `string`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/runs.ts:97](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/runs.ts#L97)

The stored signal's id, `sig_<32 hex>`.

# Interface: Validator

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/context.ts:22](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/context.ts#L22)

The parts of a Zod schema the host actually uses. Structural, so `Activity` and
`SignalDef` satisfy it without the host importing zod — and without fighting the
invariance of `z.ZodType` when the registry erases the schema's type.

url: /vlo/api/host/type-aliases/DispatcherMode.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / DispatcherMode

# Type Alias: DispatcherMode

> **DispatcherMode** = `"loop"` | `"manual"`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/dispatcher.ts:58](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/dispatcher.ts#L58)

`loop` ticks on an interval and on every `kick()`. `manual` never does either: the
process it runs in has no long-lived timer to hang a tick on, so something outside —
a cron hitting `POST /v1/timers/tick` — decides when the outbox moves.

`kick()` stays a no-op in `manual` mode on purpose. A kick is unattended and unbounded:
inside a serverless request it would start work the platform is free to freeze the moment
the response is sent, leaving tasks marked `running` with nobody behind them. `Host.drain`
(or `POST /v1/timers/tick?drain=1`) is the explicit, awaited, time-boxed form of the same
thing — the caller stays alive for it and knows when it stopped.

---

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / EventSource

# Type Alias: EventSource

> **EventSource** = [`EventInput`](../interfaces/EventInput.md) | ((`tx`, `run`) => `Promise`<[`EventInput`](../interfaces/EventInput.md) | `null`>)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transition.ts:61](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transition.ts#L61)

The event to submit. A function form runs inside the transaction with the run already
locked, so it can read and write journal rows before deciding — returning `null` commits
whatever it did without folding anything.

{ `delay_ms?`: `undefined`; `next_attempt?`: `undefined`; `retry`: `false`; }

#### delay_ms?

> `optional` **delay_ms?**: `undefined`

Never set.

#### next_attempt?

> `optional` **next_attempt?**: `undefined`

Never set.

#### retry

> **retry**: `false`

Give up.

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / Role

# Type Alias: Role

> **Role** = `"orchestrator"` | `"api"` | `` `worker:${string}` ``

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/context.ts:93](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/context.ts#L93)

One of the engine's roles: `orchestrator` moves the outbox, `api` serves the control
plane, `worker:<queue>` runs that queue's activities in-process and accepts pushes for it.

url: /vlo/api/host/functions/applyEvent.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / applyEvent

# Function: applyEvent()

> **applyEvent**(`ctx`, `runId`, `source`, `after?`): `Promise`<[`TxOutcome`](../interfaces/TxOutcome.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transition.ts:81](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/transition.ts#L81)

Submits one event. Owns its transaction, recovers a reducer throw or a divergence into
the matching marker, then runs the post-commit work (buffered signals, emits, kick).

A `ReducerFailed` is swallowed: the run is failed with an `app_error` marker and that
outcome is returned. A `Nondeterminism` is recorded as a marker and then rethrown.

## Parameters

### ctx

[`HostContext`](../interfaces/HostContext.md)

### runId

`string`

### source

[`EventSource`](../type-aliases/EventSource.md)

### after?

[`AfterApply`](../type-aliases/AfterApply.md)

## Returns

`Promise`<[`TxOutcome`](../interfaces/TxOutcome.md)>

## Throws

[RunNotFound](../classes/RunNotFound.md) when no run has that id.

## Throws

[RunTerminal](../classes/RunTerminal.md) when the run ended and the event is not a task result or a closing marker.

## Throws

[WorkflowRejected](../classes/WorkflowRejected.md) when the run's workflow is not registered on this host.

## Throws

[IllegalEvent](../classes/IllegalEvent.md) when the kernel refuses the event for a reason other than a duplicate.

## Throws

[Nondeterminism](../classes/Nondeterminism.md) after journaling the divergence.

# Function: completeTask()

> **completeTask**(`ctx`, `taskId`, `attempt`, `output`, `usage?`): `Promise`<[`TaskResult`](../interfaces/TaskResult.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/complete.ts:34](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/complete.ts#L34)

Records an attempt's output. Validated against the registered activity's output schema

url: /vlo/api/host/functions/createClient.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / createClient

# Function: createClient()

> **createClient**(`options?`): [`Client`](../interfaces/Client.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/client/index.ts:158](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/client/index.ts#L158)

Builds a [Client](../interfaces/Client.md). With no options it talks to `http://vlo.localhost` over
`globalThis.fetch`, which is only useful together with `fetch: host.fetch`.

## Parameters

### options?

[`ClientOptions`](../interfaces/ClientOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

[`Client`](../interfaces/Client.md)

## Example

```ts
import { createClient } from "@oona/vlo/host";

const client = createClient({ baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:4100", token: "control-plane-token" });
const run = await client.start(pipeline, { clip: "reel" });
await client.signal(run.run_id, "approve", { by: "me" });
const done = await client.waitFor(run.run_id, "completed");
console.log(done.output);
```

---
url: /vlo/api/host/functions/createHost.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / createHost

# Function: createHost()

> **createHost**(`options`): [`Host`](../interfaces/Host.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts:159](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts#L159)

Builds a host without binding a port or starting it. Nothing is loaded or migrated until
`start()` (or the first `fetch`). A `journal` given as a URL is opened here and closed by
`stop()`; a `Journal` instance is left to its owner.

## Parameters

### options

[`CreateHostOptions`](../interfaces/CreateHostOptions.md)

## Returns

[`Host`](../interfaces/Host.md)

## Example

```ts
import { createClient, createHost, defineWorker } from "@oona/vlo/host";

const host = createHost({
  journal: "sqlite://./.vlo/dev.db",
  workflows: [pipeline],
  activities: [render],
  workers: [defineWorker({ "pull.render": (input: { clip: string }) => ({ rendered: input.clip }) })],
});
await host.start();

const client = createClient({ fetch: host.fetch });
const run = await client.start(pipeline, { clip: "reel" });
await client.waitFor(run.run_id, "completed");
await host.stop();
```

Builds the `/v1` router for a context. Every [VloError](../classes/VloError.md) becomes a JSON error response

url: /vlo/api/host/functions/drainHost.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / drainHost

# Function: drainHost()

> **drainHost**(`ctx`, `options?`): `Promise`<[`DrainResult`](../interfaces/DrainResult.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/drain.ts:52](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/drain.ts#L52)

Ticks until a pass is quiet or the budget runs out. `Host.drain` wraps this and additionally
shares one drain between concurrent callers; call that unless you hold a `HostContext`.
Throws a plain `Error` on a context without the `orchestrator` role.

## Parameters

### ctx

[`HostContext`](../interfaces/HostContext.md)

### options?

[`DrainOptions`](../interfaces/DrainOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

`Promise`<[`DrainResult`](../interfaces/DrainResult.md)>

## Example

```ts
// Inside a request on a `manual`-mode host: carry the run as far as it goes right now.
const result = await host.drain({ maxMs: 20_000 });
if (!result.idle) console.warn(`still busy after ${result.passes} passes`);
```

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / failTask

# Function: failTask()

> **failTask**(`ctx`, `taskId`, `attempt`, `error`, `retryable?`, `cause?`, `usage?`): `Promise`<[`TaskResult`](../interfaces/TaskResult.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/complete.ts:65](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/complete.ts#L65)

Records an attempt's failure: a `retrying` event when `retryable` and the kernel's retry
plan allows another attempt, otherwise a `failed` event. The first terminal result for an
attempt wins; later ones return `duplicate: true`.

`cause` names who lost the attempt: the handler by default, the reaper on a dead lease.
`usage` is banked whichever way the attempt ends — tokens burned before a throw are spent.

## Parameters

### ctx

[`HostContext`](../interfaces/HostContext.md)

### taskId

`string`

### attempt

`number`

### error

`string`

### retryable?

`boolean` = `true`

### cause?

[`Cause`](../../index/type-aliases/Cause.md) = `"app_error"`

### usage?

[`Usage`](../../index/interfaces/Usage.md)

## Returns

`Promise`<[`TaskResult`](../interfaces/TaskResult.md)>

## Throws

[TaskNotFound](../classes/TaskNotFound.md) when no task has that id.

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / handler

# Function: handler()

> **handler**(`options`): `object`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts:341](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/roles.ts#L341)

Next route file: `export const { GET, POST } = handler({ … })`. The host is created on the
first request and shared by every request after, so a serverless function pays for the
kernel load once per instance. Pair it with `dispatcher: { mode: "manual" }` and a cron on
`POST /v1/timers/tick`.

## Parameters

### options

[`CreateHostOptions`](../interfaces/CreateHostOptions.md)

## Returns

`object`

### GET

> **GET**: [`FetchHandler`](../type-aliases/FetchHandler.md)

### POST

> **POST**: [`FetchHandler`](../type-aliases/FetchHandler.md)

## Example

```ts
// app/api/vlo/[[...path]]/route.ts
import { handler } from "@oona/vlo/host";

export const { GET, POST } = handler({
  journal: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? "sqlite://./.vlo/dev.db",
  workflows: [pipeline],
  activities: [render],
  basePath: "/api/vlo",
  dispatcher: { mode: "manual" },
});
```

url: /vlo/api/host/functions/handleTask.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / handleTask

# Function: handleTask()

> **handleTask**(`worker`, `task`, `reporter`, `options?`): `Promise`<`void`>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/handle-task.ts:45](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/worker/handle-task.ts#L45)

Runs one pushed task on a worker and reports exactly one terminal result. Heartbeats every
`heartbeat_ms`; a refused heartbeat, `timeout_ms` elapsing or `options.signal` aborting
all abort the handler's `ctx.signal`. A handler throw is reported as a retryable failure;
a missing handler as a non-retryable one. Resolves once the result was reported, and
rejects only when the reporter itself fails.

## Parameters

### worker

[`Worker`](../../index/interfaces/Worker.md)

### task

[`PushedTask`](../interfaces/PushedTask.md)

### reporter

[`TaskReporter`](../interfaces/TaskReporter.md)

### options?

[`HandleTaskOptions`](../interfaces/HandleTaskOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

`Promise`<`void`>

---

# Function: linkSecret()

> **linkSecret**(`auth`): `string` | `undefined`

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/links.ts:34](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/links.ts#L34)

The secret signed links are minted with. Falls back to the control-plane token and then
the push secret so a single-secret deployment gets links for free; `undefined` disables
them rather than signing with an empty key.

## Parameters

### auth

[`AuthConfig`](../interfaces/AuthConfig.md)

## Returns

`string` | `undefined`

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / listen

# Function: listen()

> **listen**(`handler`, `port`, `host?`): `Promise`<[`Listening`](../interfaces/Listening.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/node-server.ts:30](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/node-server.ts#L30)

Serves a fetch-style handler on `port` (`0` picks a free one) and `host` (default
`127.0.0.1`). Rejects when the port cannot be bound. Response bodies are streamed, so an
SSE response works without a framework.

## Parameters

### handler

[`FetchHandler`](../type-aliases/FetchHandler.md)

### port

`number`

### host?

`string` = `"127.0.0.1"`

## Returns

`Promise`<[`Listening`](../interfaces/Listening.md)>

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / loadKernel

# Function: loadKernel()

> **loadKernel**(): `Promise`<[`Kernel`](../interfaces/Kernel.md)>

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/load.ts:43](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/kernel/load.ts#L43)

Loads the wasm kernel once per process and returns the same instance afterwards. Looks for
`vlo_kernel_bg.wasm` in the package's `wasm/` directory, or at `VLO_KERNEL_WASM`. Rejects
when the bytes are missing or the kernel speaks a different protocol version.

## Returns

`Promise`<[`Kernel`](../interfaces/Kernel.md)>

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / openBlobStore

# Function: openBlobStore()

> **openBlobStore**(`url`): [`BlobStore`](../interfaces/BlobStore.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/blob/open.ts:15](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/blob/open.ts#L15)

Opens a blob store by URL: `file://<dir>` (relative to the working directory when the
path is) or `gcs://<bucket>/<prefix>`. The GCS client is only loaded on first use.
Throws a plain `Error` on any other scheme or an empty directory or bucket.

## Parameters

### url

`string`

## Returns

[`BlobStore`](../interfaces/BlobStore.md)

url: /vlo/api/host/functions/openJournal.md
---
[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / openJournal

# Function: openJournal()

> **openJournal**(`url`, `opts?`): [`Journal`](../interfaces/Journal.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/journal/open.ts:27](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/journal/open.ts#L27)

Opens a journal by URL: `sqlite://:memory:`, `sqlite://./.vlo/dev.db`,
`sqlite:///abs/path.db`, `postgres://…` or `postgresql://…`. Nothing is created or
migrated until `migrate()`. Throws a plain `Error` on any other scheme.

## Parameters

### url

`string`

### opts?

[`PostgresJournalOptions`](../interfaces/PostgresJournalOptions.md) = `{}`

## Returns

[`Journal`](../interfaces/Journal.md)

## Example

```ts
import { openJournal } from "@oona/vlo/host";

const journal = openJournal("postgres://user:pass@localhost/app", { schema: "vlo", max: 5 });
await journal.migrate();
const run = await journal.getRun("run_1");
await journal.close();
```

url: /vlo/api/host/functions/rebuildCheckpoint.md

[@oona/vlo](../../packages.md) / [host](../index.md) / rebuildCheckpoint

# Function: rebuildCheckpoint()

> **rebuildCheckpoint**(`ctx`, `workflow`, `run`, `events`): [`Rebuilt`](../interfaces/Rebuilt.md)

Defined in: [sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/refold.ts:103](https://github.com/oonalab/vlo/blob/a81c115e42e129b4efe8fd86066744a4f8bc3670/sdk/ts/sdk/src/host/refold.ts#L103)

Replays every input event in the journal. Kernel outputs (scheduled tasks, signal waits,
the `complete` marker) are recomputed, never re-fed.

## Parameters

### ctx

[`HostContext`](../interfaces/HostContext.md)

### workflow

[`Workflow`](../../index/interfaces/Workflow.md)

### run

[`RunRow`](../interfaces/RunRow.md)

### events

readonly [`Envelope`](../interfaces/Envelope.md)\[]

## Returns

[`Rebuilt`](../interfaces/Rebuilt.md)

## Throws

[Nondeterminism](../classes/Nondeterminism.md) at the first event whose replayed `seq` or `state_hash`
differs from the journaled one, or when `events` holds nothing foldable.
