url: /vlo/deployment.md
---
# Deployment

Vlo never owns infrastructure. A host is a Node process (or a serverless function) that
talks to your Postgres and, optionally, a bucket. `vlo deploy` renders the files your
pipeline applies; it applies nothing itself.

## The model

Three roles, any subset per process (see [concepts.md](./concepts.md#roles)):

* `orchestrator` — the dispatcher. Needs to tick: on an interval (`dispatcher.mode:
  "loop"`), or when something calls it (`"manual"`).
* `api` — the control plane and the worker callbacks.
* `worker:<queue>` — activity handlers, in-process or reached by push.

A laptop holds all three. A small self-host holds all three too. Splitting is a profile
change.

## Self-hosting on any Node host

Long-lived process, `loop` dispatcher:

```sh
VLO_PROFILE=prod PORT=8080 npx vlo serve
```

Or in code, with the same options the profile would produce:

```ts
import { serve } from "@oona/vlo/host";
import { workflows, workers, activities, signals } from "./vlo/index.ts";

const running = await serve({
  journal: process.env.DATABASE_URL!,
  blob: "gcs://my-bucket/vlo",
  workflows, workers, activities, signals,
  auth: { token: process.env.VLO_TOKEN!, pushSecret: process.env.VLO_PUSH_SECRET! },
  publicUrl: "https://vlo.example.com",
  port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8080),
});
// running.url, running.host, await running.close()
```

`serve()` binds `127.0.0.1` by default; pass `hostname: "0.0.0.0"` inside a container.
For your own listener, `createHost(options)` gives you `host.fetch: (Request) => Response`
plus `start()`, `stop()`, `tick()`, `drain()`.

Run more than one orchestrator freely: every dispatcher stage takes a claim, timers fire
exactly once, and reapers are idempotent.

## Serverless: manual dispatch

A function has no process to hang an interval on, so the orchestrator runs in
`dispatcher: { mode: "manual" }`: no timer, and `kick()` is a no-op. Progress comes from two
explicit sources.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as Request handler
  participant H as Host (manual)
  participant C as Cron
  U->>H: POST /v1/runs
  U->>H: host.drain({ maxMs })
  H->>H: tick until idle or budget spent
  U-->>U: respond
  C->>H: POST /v1/timers/tick?drain=1 (every minute)
  H-->>C: { passes, idle, counts }
```

* `Host.tick()` — one dispatcher pass. Returns
  `{ started, pushed, timers, reaped, timeouts, notified }`.
* `Host.drain({ maxMs })` — ticks until a pass moves nothing and no in-process handler is
  outstanding, or `maxMs` (default 25 s, wall clock) runs out. Returns
  `{ passes, idle, counts }`. Concurrent callers share one drain. Call it right after
  starting or signalling a run, inside the same invocation, so a chain of in-process steps
  finishes now instead of one step per cron tick.
* `POST /v1/timers/tick` — the same as `tick()` over HTTP (bearer). `?drain=1` runs
  `drain()`; `&max_ms=N` sets its budget. Served only by a process holding `orchestrator`.
* A cron hitting `POST /v1/timers/tick?drain=1` every minute is the backstop for
  invocations that died mid-drain, timers, retries and lease reaping.

Both `tick()` and `drain()` reject on a host without the `orchestrator` role.

### Who drains

With a manual dispatcher, "who drains" is a contract every caller must know. Keep it to one
rule: **the invocation that starts or signals a run drains once, after its response; the
cron tick is the backstop, never the plan.** In practice:

| Caller | Starts | Drains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request handler starting one run | `client.start` / `startFresh` | once, after the response (`after(() => host.drain({ maxMs }))`), with `maxMs` inside the route's own budget |
| Cron starting many runs | `client.start` per row with an idempotent `run_id`, inside the loop | **once, after the loop** — never per row |
| Script or test | `client.start` | `await host.drain()` inline; there is no "after the response" |
| Webhook delivering a signal | `client.signal` | once, after the response |

A cron that starts runs looks like this:

```ts
export async function POST(request: Request) {
  if (request.headers.get("authorization") !== `Bearer ${process.env.CRON_SECRET}`) return new Response(null, { status: 401 });
  const rows = await dueRows();
  for (const row of rows) {
    await client.start(weekly, { id: row.id }, { runId: `weekly_${row.id}_${isoWeek}` }); // idempotent per period
  }
  if (rows.length > 0) after(() => host.drain({ maxMs: 280_000 }));
  return new Response(null, { status: 202 });
}
```

Mounting under a framework route: `handler(options)` returns `{ GET, POST }` for a
catch-all route file and lazily creates one host per function instance. Pass `basePath`
(for example `"/api/vlo"`); the router strips it, and every URL the host hands out
(`complete_url`, signed links) includes it. `vlo doctor` warns when an orchestrator is in
`manual` mode and the profile has no `deploy.cron`.

## Splitting roles across services

Typical shape:

| Service | Roles | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control plane | `orchestrator`, `api` | Long-lived (`loop`) or serverless (`manual` + cron). Needs `publicUrl` so pushed tasks carry a `complete_url`. |
| Push workers | `worker:<queue>` | Another host with `auth.pushSecret` and `auth.callbackToken`; the control plane's profile lists the queue `url` + `secret`. |
| Pull workers | none | Any process running `runPullWorker({ baseUrl, token, worker })`; the queue is `mode: "pull"`. |

All services share the journal URL. Every control-plane route needs `auth.token`; workers
present it on callbacks.

An application with several areas registers each as a domain instead of four flat arrays:

```ts
import { defineDomain } from "@oona/vlo";
import { createHost } from "@oona/vlo/host";

export const brand = defineDomain({ name: "brand", workflows: [research, weekly], workers: [brandWorker], activities, signals });
const host = createHost({ journal, domains: [brand, media, ideas], queues: { media: { mode: "pull" } } });
```

`createHost` flattens the domains onto `workflows`, `workers`, `activities` and `signals`
(both forms may be mixed) and derives `worker:<queue>` roles from the workers as before.
Two domains with one name, or two different definitions under one workflow or activity
name, are refused at construction. Details in
[activities-and-workers.md](./activities-and-workers.md#where-workers-run).

## Postgres

Before the first boot the app's role needs `CREATE` on the database (or a DBA-provisioned
`vlo` schema it owns); see [journal.md](./journal.md#privileges-the-postgres-role-needs).

Any Postgres works, including one behind a transaction-mode pooler: the journal holds no
session state and takes no session-level locks. A run is serialised with a
transaction-scoped advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`) inside the single transaction
that folds its event, and outbox claims use `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Use the pooled
connection string on serverless. The host migrates on start and needs `CREATE` on its
schema. See [journal.md](./journal.md).

SQLite is for one process: a single writer, one file. Use it for `vlo dev`, tests and
single-node self-hosting.

## What `vlo deploy` renders

`vlo deploy --profile <name> [--out deploy/vlo] [--apply]` reads `profiles.<name>.deploy`
and writes files; `--apply` prints the commands to run. Secrets never appear in any file.
Names follow `<namePrefix>-<env>-<service>` (defaults `vlo-<env>-vlo`); the field reference
is in [configuration.md](./configuration.md#deploy).

### `target: "cloud-run"`

| File | Goes to | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cloud-run/Dockerfile` | keep | Two-stage `node:22-alpine` image. Builds `@oona/vlo`, copies `vlo.config.ts` and `src/`, sets `VLO_PROFILE`, exposes 8080, `CMD vlo serve --profile <name>`. |
| `cloud-run/cloudbuild.yaml` | keep | build → push → `gcloud run deploy`, parameterised by `_SERVICE`, `_REGION`, `_REPO`. |
| `cloud-run/cloud-run-vlo.tf` | `terraform/` | Per-env (`for_each` over `envs`) Cloud Run v2 service, service account, Secret Manager *containers* for `DATABASE_URL`, `VLO_TOKEN`, `VLO_PUSH_SECRET`, IAM bindings, `allUsers` invoker (the bearer token is the gate), `min_instance_count = 1` so the loop dispatcher keeps ticking, image under `lifecycle.ignore_changes`. Outputs `vlo_urls`. |
| `cloud-run/cloudbuild-vlo.tf` | `terraform/` | Artifact Registry repo, a deployer service account, one Cloud Build trigger per env on `main`; `prod` gated on manual approval. |
| `cloud-run/README.md` | keep | The one-time setup: connect the repo to Cloud Build, copy the `.tf` files, add one secret *version* per env with `gcloud secrets versions add`, `terraform apply`, push. |

The Terraform expects a root module that already declares `local.envs` (with a `prefix`
per env), `local.env_buckets`, `var.project_id`, `var.github_owner`, `var.github_repo` and
the `google_project_service` enablements. Secret versions are deliberately not in Terraform:
a value in state is a value in every plan output.

`--apply` prints, in order: copy the `.tf` files, `terraform apply -target` for the secret
containers, `gcloud secrets versions add <namePrefix>-<env>-<secretName>-{database-url,token,push-secret}`
for each env, `terraform apply`, and the first `gcloud builds submit`.

### `target: "vercel"`

| File | Goes to | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vercel/route.ts` | `app/api/vlo/[[...path]]/route.ts` | `export const { GET, POST } = handler({ … })` with `basePath: "/api/vlo"`, `dispatcher: { mode: "manual" }`, the profile's roles and push queues, `maxDuration = 300`. Imports `workflows` and `workers` from two barrels you provide (`@/vlo/workflows`, `@/vlo/workers`), because globs cannot be bundled into a function. |
| `vercel/vercel-crons.json` | merge into `vercel.json` | `{ "crons": [{ "path": "/api/vlo/v1/timers/tick", "schedule": "<cron>" }] }`. Only rendered when the profile holds `orchestrator`. |
| `vercel/env.md` | keep | Checklist of variables to set on the project. |

Variables the route reads: `DATABASE_URL` (pooled), `VLO_TOKEN`, `VLO_PUSH_SECRET`,
`VLO_PUBLIC_URL`, one `VLO_QUEUE_<NAME>_URL` per push queue, `VLO_BUCKET` when a bucket is
configured, and `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_BASE64` for a `gcs://` blob store off Google
infrastructure. Without a bucket the blob store falls back to `file:///tmp/vlo-blobs`,
which does not survive between invocations.

`--apply` prints: copy the route, `vercel env add <NAME> production` per variable, merge the
crons file, `vercel deploy --prod`.

## Checklist before the first deploy

1. `vlo doctor --profile <name>` with the production variables exported locally.
2. `publicUrl` set on any host that pushes tasks or mints links.
3. `auth.token` set: the control plane is reachable from the internet in both templates.
4. On serverless, a cron on `POST /v1/timers/tick?drain=1`, and `drain()` after each write
   in your own handlers.
5. Workers registered for every queue: in-process, a push `url` + `secret`, or pollers.

---

---
url: /vlo/observability.md
---
# Observability

Vlo has no separate tracing store. The journal is the trace: every durable fact about a run is
one row in `events`, and the two things that are not durable — `cmd.emit` payloads and
dispatcher warnings — go over an in-memory side channel. Source: `src/host/**`.

## The journal is the trace

Each event carries enough to reconstruct what happened and why:

| Field | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| `seq` | Position in the run. Strictly increasing, assigned by the kernel under the run lock. |
| `kind` / `status` | Which step type moved (`task`, `timer`, `signal`, `child`, `marker`) and to which of the seven statuses. |
| `step_id` / `attempt` | Which step, which attempt. Task ids are `<run_id>:<step_id>`, idempotency keys `<run_id>:<step_id>:<attempt>`. |
| `cause` | Why an attempt or run stopped: `timeout`, `heartbeat_lost`, `app_error`, `user_cancel`, `schema_violation`, `nondeterminism_detected`. |
| `error` | Free text from the worker or reducer. Never interpreted by the kernel. |
| `usage` | What this attempt spent (`cpu_ms`, `tokens`, `cost_micro_usd`). Present only when the worker reported any. |
| `ts_ms` / `random` | The clock and entropy the transition saw. A replay sees the same values. |
| `state_hash` | Hash of the state after this transition. Every event in one transition carries the same hash. |
| `schema_ref` | `name@<content hash>` of the activity or signal schema in force. |
| `parent_run_id` / `parent_step_id` | Set on every event of a child run from birth, so a run tree is a join. |

Read it with `GET /v1/runs/{id}/events`, `client.events(runId, since)`, or straight from the
table. Lifecycle events (`scheduled`, `running`, `retrying`, `cancelled`) sit next to the
reducer-facing ones, so the timeline includes dispatch, lease and retry decisions, not just
results.

Markers are the run-level punctuation: `start` (the input), `complete` (the output),
`continue` (the next input), `cancel`, `fail` (a reducer throw; its payload is the event that
was being folded, since that event's own transaction rolled back) and `nondeterminism`.

## Usage accounting

Usage travels one way and is banked once:

1. A handler calls `ctx.reportUsage({ tokens?, costMicroUsd?, cpuMs? })` as often as it
   likes; the worker tallies per attempt (integers, never negative).
2. The tally rides on the attempt's result — the `complete` or `fail` body over HTTP, the
   reporter call in-process — and lands as `usage` on the `task/succeeded`, `task/failed` or
   `task/retrying` event.
3. The kernel adds it to `kernel_state.usage_total` while folding, on lifecycle events too,
   so a retried attempt's spend is not lost.
4. Every reducer event carries `usage_total` (the banked total including this event);
   `task_done` also carries the step's own `usage`, zeroed when nothing was reported.

A reducer can therefore decide on a budget without keeping its own tally; that is how the
agent layer parks a run on a top-up signal. The current total is also readable off the
checkpoint: `run_state.kernel_state` is JSON with a `usage_total` field. `cost_micro_usd` is
whatever the worker reports; the engine has no price table, and child runs are not rolled up
into their parent.

## The side channel

`host.events` is a Node `EventEmitter`. Nothing on it is journaled or replayed.

| Channel | Payload | Emitted when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `emit` | `{ run_id, channel, data }` | A transition committed with `cmd.emit(channel, data)` commands. Also relayed on the SSE stream as `event: emit`. |
| `warning` | `{ message, error? }` | The dispatcher could not start, push, fire, reap or notify something, or a poll accept failed. Never thrown, never printed; subscribe if you want a log. |
| `task_scheduled` | `{ run_id, task_id, queue }` | A task row was committed. Wakes an open `POST /v1/tasks/poll` for that queue. |

```ts
host.events.on("warning", ({ message, error }) => console.warn("vlo", message, error));
```

A closed journal during shutdown is not reported as a warning; the dispatcher drops it.

## Following a run live

`client.stream(runId, { since?, signal? })` yields `journal`, `emit` and finally `end`
messages over the SSE form of the events route (see [HTTP API](http-api.md)). Journal frames
are a replay plus a tail, so reconnecting with the last `seq` loses nothing durable; emits
between connections are gone. `client.waitFor(runId, status)` is the polling alternative
for scripts and tests.

## Health and the outbox

* `GET /healthz` answers `{ ok, roles, workflows }` with no auth; it says the process is up
  and what it serves, nothing about the journal.
* `POST /v1/timers/tick` answers `TickCounts` — `started`, `pushed`, `timers`, `reaped`,
  `timeouts`, `notified` — for one dispatcher pass, and `?drain=1` answers
  `{ passes, idle, counts }`. A cron that logs these has a per-minute picture of how much the
  outbox moved and whether it ran dry (`idle: true`) or hit its time box.
* `vlo doctor --profile <name> [--json]` runs real round trips: journal connect, migrate and
  commit; blob put/get; kernel wasm size and protocol; schema registration; each push queue's
  `/healthz`; roles against dispatcher mode. It exits 1 on any failing check. The hint
  strings are listed in [errors](errors.md).

## Nondeterminism as a correctness signal

On every fold the host re-hashes the stored checkpoint and compares it with the stored
`state_hash`; when the checkpoint is missing or was written by another bundle it folds the
journal from `seq 0` and compares each transition's hash with the hash journaled on the
trigger event. The first disagreement ends the run: a `nondeterminism` marker with
`cause: nondeterminism_detected` and the divergent `seq` in `error`, and every open task is
cancelled. Treat it as a bug report, not a flake — the reducer no longer reproduces the
history it wrote (a `Date`, `Math.random`, or a state shape change without
`continue_as_new`). It is never retried.

## Not built yet

Everything below would be an additive reader over the journal; none of it needs a kernel or
schema change.

* **OpenTelemetry export.** A run maps to a trace and a step to a span: `started_at_ms` /
  `closed_at_ms` bound the trace, `scheduled` → terminal events bound each span, `cause` and
  `error` become span status, `usage` becomes attributes, `parent_run_id` links traces.
* **A console.** Run tree, inbox of `awaiting_signal` runs, event timeline, rewind and fork.
  Today the inbox is `GET /v1/runs?status=awaiting_signal`.
* **`assignee` search attribute.** The `runs.assignee` column exists and is not written or
  queried yet.
* **Child usage roll-up.** `usage_total` is per run; a parent does not see what its children
  spent.
* **Pending-migration and schema-drift detection in `vlo doctor`.** It reports schemas that
  are absent, not ones that differ.

---

---
url: /vlo/http-api.md
---
# HTTP API

The host exposes one `(Request) => Response` handler (`host.fetch`), so the same routes serve
from a Node port (`serve()`), a framework route file (`handler()`), or a test with no socket
at all (`createClient({ fetch: host.fetch })`). Source: `src/host/api/**`, `src/client/**`.

## Conventions

* **JSON in, JSON out.** Bodies are `application/json`; an empty body is `null`. A failed
  request answers `{ "error": { "code": string, "message": string } }` with the status the
  error carries (see [errors](errors.md)); anything unexpected is `500` with code `internal`.
* **Auth.** When `auth.token` is configured, every control-plane route needs
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (compared timing-safe) and answers `401 unauthorized`
  otherwise. Two exceptions: `POST /v1/tasks/push` is authenticated by an HMAC over the body,
  and the signal route accepts a signed link token in `?token=`. Without `auth.token` the
  host is open.
* **Roles.** A route belongs to a role. A host that does not hold it answers
  `404 role_not_served`; an unknown path is `404 no_route`.
* **`basePath`.** A host mounted under a prefix (for example `/api/vlo`) strips it before
  matching, so routes are always written as `/v1/…`. A path without the prefix is matched as
  it stands, which is what lets an in-process client keep calling `/v1/runs`. Every URL the
  host hands out (`complete_url`, signed links, the confirmation form's action) carries the
  prefix.
* **`/healthz`** needs no token and no role.

## Routes

| Method | Path | Role | Auth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/healthz` | any | none |
| `POST` | `/v1/runs` | `api` | bearer |
| `GET` | `/v1/runs` | `api` | bearer |
| `GET` | `/v1/runs/{id}` | `api` | bearer |
| `GET` | `/v1/runs/{id}/events` | `api` | bearer |
| `POST` | `/v1/runs/{id}/signals/{name}` | `api` | bearer, or `?token=` |
| `GET` | `/v1/runs/{id}/signals/{name}?token=` | `api` | link token |
| `POST` | `/v1/runs/{id}/links/{name}` | `api` | bearer |
| `POST` | `/v1/runs/{id}/cancel` | `api` | bearer |
| `POST` | `/v1/tasks/poll` | `api` | bearer |
| `POST` | `/v1/tasks/{id}/complete` | `api` | bearer |
| `POST` | `/v1/tasks/{id}/fail` | `api` | bearer |
| `POST` | `/v1/tasks/{id}/heartbeat` | `api` | bearer |
| `POST` | `/v1/tasks/push` | `worker:*` | HMAC |
| `POST` | `/v1/timers/tick` | `orchestrator` | bearer |

### `GET /healthz`

`200 { "ok": true, "roles": string[], "workflows": string[] }`. `vlo doctor` probes each push
queue's `/healthz` to decide whether a worker host is reachable.

### `POST /v1/runs`

Request `{ "workflow": string, "input"?: Json, "run_id"?: string, "search"?: object }`.
Response `201 { "run_id": string }`. Unknown workflow → `400 unknown_workflow`. The row is
written with `status: "created"`; the dispatcher's next pass folds `started`, so on a
`manual` dispatcher the run stays `created` until something ticks. `run_id` defaults to
`run_<32 hex>`; passing your own makes a duplicate submission idempotent (the insert is
`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`).

### `GET /v1/runs?status=&workflow=&limit=`

`200 RunView[]`, newest first, default limit 50, scoped to the host's namespace. `RunView`:

```json
{ "run_id": "run_…", "workflow": "example", "status": "awaiting_signal", "last_seq": 7,
  "search": {}, "created_at_ms": 0, "updated_at_ms": 0, "started_at_ms": 0,
  "closed_at_ms": 0, "parent_run_id": "run_…", "continued_from": "run_…",
  "continued_to": "run_…", "output": null, "error": "…", "cause": "app_error" }
```

`started_at_ms`, `closed_at_ms`, `parent_run_id`, `continued_from`, `continued_to` and
`output` are present only when set. `error` and `cause` are present only on a `failed` run:
the `error` of its closing marker (the reducer's `WorkflowFailure` message, or the refold
mismatch) and that marker's cause (`app_error` or `nondeterminism_detected`). A `continued` run's result lives on the run named by
`continued_to`; follow the chain to its end.
`status` is one of `created`, `running`, `awaiting_signal`, `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, `continued`.

### `GET /v1/runs/{id}`

`200 RunView`; `404 run_not_found`.

### `GET /v1/runs/{id}/events?since=N`

`200 Envelope[]` with `seq > N`, ascending (default `N = 0`). Each envelope is one journal
row: `run_id`, `seq`, `step_id`, `attempt`, `kind`, `status`, `cause?`, `usage?`, `ts_ms`,
`random`, `schema_ref?`, `payload?`, `payload_ref?`, `error?`, `parent_run_id?`,
`parent_step_id?`, `state_hash`.

With `Accept: text/event-stream` or `?stream=1` the same route answers as Server-Sent Events
(`Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`,
`X-Accel-Buffering: no`):

```
id: 3
event: journal
data: {"run_id":"run_…","seq":3,…}

event: emit
data: {"channel":"human","data":{…}}

: keepalive

event: end
data: {"run_id":"run_…","status":"completed",…}
```

* `journal` frames replay everything after `since`, then follow the journal every
  `streamPollMs` (default 500 ms). `id` is the `seq`.
* `emit` frames carry `cmd.emit` payloads for this run. They are in-memory only: a reconnect
  resumes the journal, not the emits it missed.
* `: keepalive` is sent every 15 s.
* `end` carries the final `RunView` once the run is terminal and every event has been sent.
* Resume with `?since=` or the `Last-Event-ID` header; `?since` wins when both are present.

### `POST /v1/runs/{id}/signals/{name}`

Request: the signal payload as the body (any JSON; empty body = `null`). If the host has a
`signal()` definition of that name registered, the payload is validated first
(`400 bad_request` on a mismatch). Response `200 { "signal_id": "sig_…", "delivered": bool }`.
`delivered: false` means either no wait was open (the signal is buffered and delivered when
one opens) or the matching wait had already closed because its deadline fired or the run
ended (the signal is recorded and never folded).

With `?token=<signed link>` no bearer is needed. The same path with `GET` and a valid token
renders an HTML confirmation form (`Cache-Control: no-store`) whose submit POSTs the token
back; a `GET` never delivers. An invalid or expired token falls through to the bearer check
and gets the same `401` as no credential at all.

### `POST /v1/runs/{id}/links/{name}`

Request `{ "expires_in_ms"?: integer }` (default 7 days). Response
`200 { "url": string, "expires_at_ms": number }`. The URL is
`<publicUrl or request origin><basePath>/v1/runs/{id}/signals/{name}?token=v1.<expiry>.<hmac>`.
`503 links_disabled` when the host has none of `auth.linkSecret`, `auth.token`,
`auth.pushSecret`.

### `POST /v1/runs/{id}/cancel`

Appends the `cancel` marker (`cause: user_cancel`), closes every open step and cancels open
tasks. Response `200 RunView`. Cancelling a terminal run is a no-op that still answers `200`.

### `POST /v1/tasks/poll`

The pull half of delivery. Request `{ "queue": string, "worker_id": string, "wait_ms"?: 0–25000,
"max"?: 1–10 }`; out-of-range values are clamped. The host claims up to `max` scheduled tasks
on that queue, records each as `running` with a lease, and answers `200 { "tasks": PushedTask[] }`.
With nothing to hand out it holds the request open up to `wait_ms`, re-checking every 500 ms
and waking early when a transition in this process commits a task for the queue.
`runPullWorker` in `@oona/vlo/host` is the client loop.

### Task callbacks

All three take `{ "attempt": integer, … }`; `attempt` must match the attempt the worker was
given. `404 task_not_found` for an unknown id.

| Route | Body | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `…/complete` | `{ attempt, output?: Json, usage?: Usage }` | `200 { "duplicate": bool }` |
| `…/fail` | `{ attempt, error: string, retryable?: bool = true, cause?: Cause, usage?: Usage }` | `200 { "duplicate": bool }` |
| `…/heartbeat` | `{ attempt }` | `200 { "ok": true }`; `410 lease_lost` if the attempt no longer holds its lease |

`Usage` is `{ "cpu_ms": int, "tokens": int, "cost_micro_usd": int }` (missing fields are 0).
`duplicate: true` means this attempt already produced a terminal result, or the task moved on
to a later attempt, and nothing was written. On `complete`, the output is validated against
the registered activity's output schema; a mismatch is recorded as `failed` with
`cause: schema_violation`, which the kernel never retries. On `fail` with `retryable: true`,
the kernel plans the next attempt from the task's retry policy and the attempt is either
`retrying` (back in the outbox after the delay) or `failed` for good.

### `POST /v1/tasks/push`

Inbound delivery for a worker role. The body is a `PushedTask`:

```json
{ "task_id": "run_x:task#1", "run_id": "run_x", "step_id": "task#1", "attempt": 1,
  "activity": { "name": "example.plan", "schema_ref": "example.plan@<hash>" },
  "idempotency_key": "run_x:task#1:1", "input": {…}, "lease_ms": 60000,
  "heartbeat_ms": 20000, "timeout_ms": 240000, "complete_url": "https://…/v1/tasks/run_x%3Atask%231" }
```

Headers: `vlo-task-id`, `vlo-attempt`, `vlo-timestamp` (ms), and
`vlo-signature: v1=hmac-sha256(secret, "<task_id>.<attempt>.<ts>.<sha256(body)>")` in hex.
The receiver rejects a signature older or newer than 5 minutes. Responses:

| Status | Meaning to the pusher |
| --- | --- |
| `202` | Accepted; the result arrives later on `complete_url`. |
| `200 { "output": … }` | Accepted with an inline result (contract only; the SDK worker always answers 202). |
| `409 { "duplicate": true }` | Already running this idempotency key in this process; treated as accepted. |
| `401` | Bad signature. Retried later (`401`, `403`, `408`, `429` mean "not now"). |
| `404 no_handler` | No worker here serves the activity. Fatal: the task is failed with `schema_violation`. |
| `503 no_push_secret` | This host has no `auth.pushSecret`. Retried later. |

The handler runs after the `202` is sent; results go to `complete_url` with the host's
`auth.callbackToken` (falling back to `auth.token`) as the bearer.

### `POST /v1/timers/tick`

One dispatcher pass: start created runs, push scheduled tasks, fire due timers, reap lapsed
leases, reap timed-out attempts, notify parents of closed children. Response
`200 { "started", "pushed", "timers", "reaped", "timeouts", "notified" }` (counts). With
`?drain=1[&max_ms=N]` the host keeps ticking until a pass moves nothing and no in-process
handler is outstanding, or `max_ms` (default 25 000) runs out, and answers
`200 { "passes": n, "idle": bool, "counts": TickCounts }`. This is the cron's entry point on a
`manual` dispatcher; a host without the `orchestrator` role answers `404 role_not_served`.

## The client

`createClient({ baseUrl?, token?, fetch? })` from `@oona/vlo/host` wraps every route above.
Lifted from the test suite:

```ts
import { createClient, serve } from "@oona/vlo/host";

const server = await serve({ journal: "sqlite://.vlo/dev.db", workflows: [exampleWorkflow],
  activities: [plan, work, finish], signals: [approve], workers: [worker],
  auth: { token: TOKEN }, port: 0 });

const client = createClient({ baseUrl: server.url, token: TOKEN });
const started = await client.start(exampleWorkflow, { n: 2 });

for await (const message of client.stream(started.run_id)) {
  if (message.type === "journal") console.log(message.seq, message.data.kind);
  if (message.type === "end") console.log(message.data.status);
}

await client.waitFor(started.run_id, "awaiting_signal");
await client.signal(started.run_id, approve, { by: "sse" });
```

`client.start` returns the `RunView` (it calls `GET` after the `POST`); `events`, `get`,
`list`, `cancel`, `signalLink` map one-to-one onto the routes; `waitFor(runId, status,
timeoutMs = 10_000)` polls every 50 ms. A non-2xx answer rejects with
`"<METHOD> <path> → <status> <body>"`, except `find(runId)`, which answers `null` on a 404.

`startFresh(workflow, input, { runId, search?, maxChain = 50 })` is `start` for a unit of
work that may run more than once: it walks `runId`, `${runId}_2`, `${runId}_3`, … and starts
the first id with no run, or joins (returns) a live one. The result is
`{ run, joined }`. The walk is deterministic, so two concurrent callers land on the same id
and the insert's `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` makes one of them the joiner. For "once ever" or
"once per period" ids, plain `start` with a fixed `runId` is already idempotent.

---

---
url: /vlo/journal.md
---
# Journal

The journal is the only durable state Vlo has. It is the source of truth for every run and,
because the `tasks` table doubles as an outbox with leases, it is also the queue. There is no
broker: a transition commits its events, its checkpoint and its new task rows together, and
the dispatcher picks the rows up on its next pass. Source: `src/journal/**`, `src/blob/**`.

## Tables

All tables live in their own Postgres schema (`vlo` by default) or, on SQLite, unprefixed in
their own file. Every instant is a `bigint` / `INTEGER` millisecond epoch named `*_ms`.

| Table | Key columns | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runs` | `run_id` PK, `namespace`, `workflow`, `component_digest`, `status`, `last_seq`, `parent_run_id`, `parent_step_id`, `continued_from`, `continued_to`, `input` / `input_ref`, `output` / `output_ref`, `search`, `assignee`, `created_at_ms`, `updated_at_ms`, `started_at_ms`, `closed_at_ms`, `parent_notified_at_ms`, `start_claimed_until_ms`, `notify_claimed_until_ms` | One row per run. `status = 'created'` rows and closed-but-unnotified children are outbox stages. |
| `events` | `(run_id, seq)` PK, `step_id`, `attempt`, `kind`, `status`, `cause`, `schema_ref`, `payload` / `payload_ref`, `error`, `usage`, `random`, `state_hash`, `parent_run_id`, `parent_step_id`, `ts_ms` | Append-only history. The primary key is the backstop against a double append. |
| `run_state` | `run_id` PK, `seq`, `bundle_digest`, `kernel_state`, `state` / `state_ref`, `state_hash` | The checkpoint. Rewritten on every transition in the same transaction as the events. Exactly one of `state` / `state_ref` (CHECK constraint). |
| `tasks` | `task_id` PK, `run_id`, `step_id`, `attempt`, `activity`, `schema_ref`, `queue`, `input` / `input_ref`, `retry_policy`, `status`, `idempotency_key` UNIQUE, `not_before_ms`, `dispatched_at_ms`, `dispatch_attempts`, `dispatch_claimed_until_ms`, `lease_ttl_ms`, `lease_until_ms`, `worker_id`, `heartbeat_at_ms`, `timeout_ms` | The outbox and the lease. `UNIQUE (run_id, step_id)`; one row per step, rewritten per attempt. |
| `timers` | `(run_id, step_id)` PK, `fire_at_ms`, `fired_at_ms`, `claimed_until_ms` | Due timers, claimed and fired by the dispatcher. Deduped by `step_id`. |
| `signal_waits` | `(run_id, step_id)` PK, `name`, `schema_ref`, `expires_at_ms` | Open `await_signal` steps. `expires_at_ms` is informational; a wait with a deadline also owns a `timers` row named `<step_id>:timeout`. |
| `signals` | `signal_id` PK, `run_id`, `name`, `payload` / `payload_ref`, `sender`, `created_at_ms`, `delivered_at_ms`, `delivered_step_id` | The inbox. A signal with no matching wait stays undelivered until one opens. |
| `schemas` | `(name, version)` PK, `json_schema`, `retry_policy`, `created_at_ms` | Activity and signal schemas, keyed by content hash. Upserted on host boot. |
| `bundles` | `digest` PK, `workflow`, `kind`, `blob_ref`, `source_map_ref`, `created_at_ms` | Reserved for workflow bundles; the table exists and is not written yet. |
| `migrations` | `version` PK, `applied_at_ms` | Which migration files have run. |

### Outbox and lease columns on `tasks`

| Predicate | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status = 'scheduled' AND dispatched_at_ms IS NULL AND not_before_ms <= now` | Waiting to be pushed or polled. A crash between commit and push loses nothing: the row is still here. |
| `dispatch_claimed_until_ms > now` | Claimed by one dispatcher pass; other passes skip it until the hold lapses (30 s by default). |
| `dispatch_attempts` | Incremented per claim; drives the exponential backoff after a refused push. |
| `status = 'running' AND lease_until_ms < now` | Lease lapsed without a heartbeat; the reaper fails the attempt with `cause: heartbeat_lost`. |
| `status = 'running' AND dispatched_at_ms + timeout_ms < now` | Attempt outlived its wall-clock budget; the reaper fails it with `cause: timeout`. |

### Text, not jsonb

Anything that is hashed or replayed — `run_state.state`, `run_state.kernel_state`,
`events.payload`, `runs.input`, `runs.output`, `tasks.input`, `schemas.retry_policy` — is stored
as `text`, byte-exact. `jsonb` rewrites key order and numeric lexemes, which would change the
bytes the kernel hashes and break the re-fold check. Only `runs.search`, `events.usage` and
`tasks.retry_policy` are `jsonb` on Postgres (plain `TEXT` on SQLite).

## Postgres adapter

`src/journal/postgres.ts`, driver `pg`, options `{ schema?: string, max?: number }`.

* **Own schema.** Every table is created unqualified inside `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS vlo`.
  Nothing in the journal can reach `public`, so it coexists with whatever else uses the
  database.
* **Migrations on boot.** `host.start()` (and therefore `serve()`, `handler()` and the first
  `host.fetch`) calls `journal.migrate()`. `vlo doctor` does the same unless `--no-migrate`
  is given. The migration lock is a transaction-scoped advisory lock on `vlo:migrate`, so
  several processes may boot at once.
* **Session-free.** The adapter keeps no session state at all: no startup `options`, no
  session-level `SET`, no session advisory locks. Every read and every transaction is
  `BEGIN` · `SET LOCAL search_path TO <schema>` · statements · `COMMIT` on a pooled
  connection. Per-run serialisation is `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0))` on
  the key `vlo:run:<run_id>`, released at commit. Claims use `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so
  concurrent dispatcher passes get disjoint rows.
* **Why it works behind transaction-mode poolers.** PgBouncer in transaction mode, PlanetScale
  and Neon's poolers multiplex sessions and reject startup parameters. Because the journal
  never assumes the next statement lands on the same backend, and everything it sets is
  `LOCAL` to one transaction, it is correct behind any of them.
* Placeholders are written once as `?` and rewritten to `$n` for Postgres.

## SQLite adapter

`src/journal/sqlite.ts`, built on `node:sqlite` (Node ≥ 22.5), no native dependency.

* One file, one connection, one writer. A promise mutex owns the connection: a transaction
  holds it from `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` to `COMMIT`; reads queue behind it. `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
  takes the write lock up front, which is what makes claims disjoint without `SKIP LOCKED`.
* Pragmas on open: `journal_mode = WAL`, `busy_timeout = 5000`, `foreign_keys = ON`.
* The directory of the file is created on demand, so `vlo doctor` and `vlo serve` work on a
  fresh checkout. `sqlite://:memory:` gives a throwaway journal for tests.
* Share one `SqliteJournal` instance per process. Separate processes on the same file are
  serialised by SQLite's lock and `busy_timeout`.

## URL forms

| URL | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| `sqlite://:memory:` | In-memory SQLite, gone when the process exits. |
| `sqlite://.vlo/dev.db` | SQLite file at a relative path: relative to the config file's directory when it comes from a profile, to the working directory when passed to `openJournal` or `serve` directly. |
| `sqlite:///abs/path.db` | SQLite file at an absolute path. |
| `postgres://…` or `postgresql://…` | Postgres via `pg`; the rest of the URL is passed to the driver. |

`openJournal(url, { schema?, max? })` in `@oona/vlo/host` picks the adapter by prefix and throws
`unsupported journal url: …` otherwise.

### Privileges the Postgres role needs

The first boot does two things in order: create the schema (`vlo` by default), then create
the tables inside it. Each needs one privilege, and the two are on different objects:

| Step | Needs | Granted by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CREATE SCHEMA vlo` | `CREATE` on the **database** | `GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE <db> TO <role>;` |
| tables and indexes in `vlo` | `CREATE` on the **schema** | automatic for the schema's owner; otherwise `GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA vlo TO <role>;` |

Pick one of two setups:

* **Let the app own the schema (simplest).** Grant `CREATE` on the database once. The app
  creates `vlo` on first boot, owns it, and needs nothing else afterwards. Steady-state runtime
  only needs `USAGE` on the schema and DML on its tables, which the owner has.
* **DBA-provisioned schema.** If the role may not have database-level `CREATE`, have an admin run
  `CREATE SCHEMA vlo AUTHORIZATION <role>;` once. The host sees the schema and skips creation.

Do not mix them by creating the schema as a *different* role: the app is then not the owner and
fails on the first table with `permission denied for schema vlo` until it also receives
`USAGE, CREATE` on the schema.

Diagnostics, run as an admin on the same database the app connects to:

```sql
SELECT usename, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename LIKE '%' GROUP BY 1;  -- who is actually connected
SELECT has_database_privilege('<role>', current_database(), 'CREATE');             -- step 1
SELECT has_schema_privilege('<role>', 'vlo', 'CREATE');                            -- step 2
SELECT version FROM vlo.migrations ORDER BY 1;                                     -- what the boot achieved
```

Behind a pooler the login name can carry routing information (PlanetScale uses
`<role>.<branch>`); the Postgres role is the part the pooler maps it to, which
`pg_stat_activity` shows. Grant to that name. `vlo doctor` prints these remedies when a boot
fails on either privilege.

## Migrations

Migrations are SQL strings inlined as TypeScript modules, one per dialect and version, listed
in `MIGRATION_VERSIONS` (`src/journal/migrations.ts`):

| Version | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `0001_init` | Every table above and its indexes. |
| `0002_task_timeout` | `tasks.timeout_ms` and the `tasks_timeout_idx` partial index behind the timeout reaper. |
| `0003_continued_to` | `runs.continued_to`, the forward link written when `continue_as_new` starts a successor. |

The runner reads `migrations`, applies whatever is missing inside the caller's transaction
and inserts the bookkeeping row. Postgres statements are `IF NOT EXISTS` and rerunnable;
SQLite's `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` in `0002` and `0003` is guarded only by the `migrations`
row, so do not delete that table on SQLite.

## Blob stores

Anything over the inline limit — `INLINE_LIMIT_BYTES`, 256 KiB — leaves the journal and is
stored content-addressed. The journal keeps a reference of the form `blob://sha256/<64 hex>`
in the matching `*_ref` column (`payload_ref`, `input_ref`, `output_ref`, `state_ref`).

```ts
interface BlobStore {
  /** Stores the bytes and returns their sha256, lowercase hex. Idempotent. */
  put(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<string>;
  get(sha256Hex: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
}
```

`offloadIfOversized(store, text)` returns the ref when the UTF-8 byte length exceeds the limit
and `null` otherwise; `readBlobText(store, ref)` reads it back byte-exact. The kernel decides
`state_inline` for the checkpoint; the host offloads the completion output the same way.

| URL | Store | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file://<dir>` | `FileBlobStore` | `<dir>/<first two hex>/<sha256>`; written to a temp file and renamed, so readers never see a partial blob. Default is `file://.vlo/blobs`; a relative directory resolves like a SQLite path (config directory from a profile, working directory when opened directly). |
| `gcs://<bucket>[/<prefix>]` | `GcsBlobStore` | Object key `<prefix>/<first two hex>/<sha256>`. `put` checks existence first, so a retried offload uploads nothing. Needs the optional peer dependency `@google-cloud/storage` (^7). Credentials: Application Default Credentials, or `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_BASE64` (base64 of a service-account JSON) where no metadata server exists. |

`openBlobStore(url)` throws `unsupported blob store url: …` for any other scheme. `vlo doctor`
writes a 1 KiB probe and checks that `put` returned its real sha256 and that `get` returned
every byte.

## `JournalClosed`

Every journal call made after `close()` rejects with `JournalClosed` (`code: "journal_closed"`,
exported from `@oona/vlo/host`). Shutdown is racy by nature — a worker reporting a result while
the host stops — and this is the one recognisable error those late calls get instead of
whatever the driver does to a closed handle. The dispatcher drops it silently as "shutting
down" rather than emitting a `warning`.

## The interface

`Journal` (`src/journal/types.ts`) is what the host talks to. Reads outside a transaction:
`readEvents`, `getRun`, `getState`, `getTask`, `listTasks`, `query`, `dueTimers`,
`expiredLeases`, `expiredTimeouts`. Everything that writes goes through
`transaction(fn)` and a `JournalTx`: `lockRun`, `createRun`, `applyTransition` (the whole
kernel write-set plus the child and successor run rows the host derives, atomically), the claim methods (`claimUndispatchedTasks`,
`claimCreatedRuns`, `claimClosedUnnotified`, `claimDueTimers`), lease methods
(`markDispatched`, `deferDispatch`, `heartbeat`), timer and signal methods, and the schema
registry (`upsertSchema`, `getSchema`).

If you write another adapter, `journalConformance` from `@oona/vlo/testing` runs the same
suite the two built-in journals pass: ordering, disjoint claims, hold expiry, terminal marks,
idempotent appends. Point it at your `Journal` factory inside a Vitest `describe`.

# Errors

Three families: host errors that become HTTP responses, kernel error codes that the host
maps or passes through, and the checks `vlo doctor` prints. Source: `src/host/errors.ts`,
`crates/kernel/src/error.rs`, `src/cli/checks.ts`.

## Host errors

Every class extends `VloError` (`code`, `status`, `message`) and is exported from
`@oona/vlo/host`. A route catches it and answers `{ "error": { code, message } }` with `status`.
Anything that is not a `VloError` becomes `500 internal`.

| Class | `code` | HTTP | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RunNotFound` | `run_not_found` | 404 | No run with that id. |
| `TaskNotFound` | `task_not_found` | 404 | No task with that id on a callback. |
| `RunTerminal` | `run_terminal` | 409 | An event other than a task result or closing marker reached a completed, failed, cancelled or continued run. |
| `IllegalEvent` | kernel code, see below | 409 | The kernel refused the event. `kernelError` holds the original `{ code, message, seq?, step_id? }`. |
| `Nondeterminism` | `refold_mismatch` | 409 | The checkpoint hash or a re-fold disagreed with the journal. The run is failed first with cause `nondeterminism_detected` and a `nondeterminism` marker, then this is thrown. |
| `ReducerFailed` | `reducer_failed` | 409 | The reducer threw (`WorkflowFailure` or anything else), or a `spawn` / `continue_as_new` named a workflow this host does not know. `applyEvent` swallows it and records the `fail` marker (cause `app_error`) with the trigger event as payload; the pre-event checkpoint stays. |
| `WorkflowRejected` | `unknown_workflow` | 400 | Start, fold or spawn named a workflow this host has not registered. |
| `Unauthorized` | `unauthorized` | 401 | Missing or wrong bearer, bad push signature, bad or expired link token. |
| `BadRequest` | `bad_request` | 400 | Malformed body, missing field, invalid signal payload, bad `max_ms`. |
| `LeaseLost` | `lease_lost` | 410 | A heartbeat for an attempt that no longer holds its lease. The worker should stop. |

Routes also raise three local ones with the same shape: `role_not_served` (404, the host
lacks the role), `no_route` (404), and `links_disabled` (503, no secret to sign links with).
The push endpoint answers `503 no_push_secret`, `404 no_handler` and `409 { "duplicate": true }`
as plain JSON.

## Kernel error codes

The kernel never throws; every export returns `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, seq?,
step_id? } }`. The host wraps a refusal in `IllegalEvent`, passing the code through unchanged.
Three codes — `unknown_step`, `already_terminal`, `bad_seq` — are treated as "already folded"
(an at-least-once redelivery) and answer `duplicate: true` instead of failing.

| Code | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `malformed_json` | The input string, a payload, the reducer's state or a command's JSON does not parse. |
| `invalid_event` | Empty `run_id` or `step_id`; `random` is not 32 lowercase hex; both `payload` and `payload_ref` set; `payload_ref` without the `blob://sha256/` prefix; an unroutable kind/status/marker combination; a `payload_ref` reaching a fold unresolved; a lifecycle-only event sent to `reduce_step`; `kernel_state` missing on anything but `started`; event `run_id` differs from the run. |
| `payload_too_large` | Inline `payload` exceeds 262 144 bytes. Offload it and send `payload_ref`. |
| `run_closed` | The `RunRef` is already completed, failed, cancelled or continued. Distinct from the host's `run_terminal`, which refuses the event before the kernel is called. |
| `bad_seq` | `started` arrived while `last_seq` is not 0. |
| `unknown_step` | No open step with that id (terminal steps are pruned, so a late duplicate lands here, as does the loser of a signal-versus-deadline race). |
| `illegal_transition` | Step kind does not match the event kind; the status edge is not in the step machine; an event for a higher attempt than the step's; a retry that skips attempts; `started` on a run that is not `created`; a signal for a step not `awaiting_signal`. |
| `already_terminal` | An event for a lower attempt than the step's, or a retry naming an attempt the step already reached. |
| `invalid_command` | Empty activity, workflow, signal name, emit channel or explicit step id; a timer with neither `fire_at_ms` nor `fire_in_ms`. |
| `duplicate_step_id` | A command's explicit `id` names a step that is still open. |
| `multiple_completions` | A reduction contains more than one `complete` / `continue_as_new`. |
| `commands_after_completion` | Any command follows a `complete` / `continue_as_new` in the same reduction. |

## Authoring and runtime errors

| Class | Package | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ActivityInputError` | `@oona/vlo` | `cmd.task(activity, input)` was given input that fails the activity's Zod input schema. Thrown synchronously inside the reducer, which fails the run. |
| `WorkflowFailure` | `@oona/vlo` | The deliberate way to fail a run from a reducer: `throw new WorkflowFailure(message, details?)`. `sequence` throws it for a task that did not succeed and for a `waitFor` deadline with `onTimeout: "fail"`. |
| `JournalClosed` | `@oona/vlo/host` | Any journal call after `close()`. `code: "journal_closed"`. Expected during shutdown. |
| `LeaseLost` | `@oona/vlo/host` | See above; also surfaces to a worker as a rejected `ctx.heartbeat()`, after which `ctx.signal` is aborted. |

## `vlo doctor`

Each check is a real round trip and prints `✓`, `⚠` or `✗` with a hint under anything that is
not `✓`. Any `✗` sets exit code 1. `--json` prints the same `Check[]`.

| Check | Status | Hint | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `journal` | ✗ | `journal must be a sqlite:// or postgres:// url` | Fix `profile.journal`. |
| `journal` | ✗ | `check the journal url and that the database is reachable` | The empty write transaction failed after a successful migrate; check network and credentials. |
| `journal` | ✗ | `the schema may be missing; re-run without --no-migrate` | You skipped migrations and the tables do not exist yet. |
| `migrate` | ⚠ | `re-run without --no-migrate to apply pending migrations` | Informational when `--no-migrate` was passed. |
| `migrate` | ✗ | `the journal is unreachable: check the url, host and port, and that the database is running` | Connection refused or timed out. |
| `migrate` | ✗ | `the journal rejected the credentials in the url` | Wrong user or password. |
| `migrate` | ✗ | `the database named in the url does not exist` | Create it, or fix the URL. |
| `migrate` | ✗ | `the journal user needs CREATE on its schema` | Grant `CREATE` on the database so `CREATE SCHEMA vlo` can run. |
| `blob` | ✗ | `the store is not content-addressed; payload refs would not resolve` | `put` returned something other than the sha256 of the bytes; your store breaks the contract. |
| `blob` | ✗ | `the store is truncating writes` | `get` returned fewer bytes than were written. |
| `blob` | ✗ | `check the blob url and that the process may write there` | Bad URL, missing peer dependency for `gcs://`, or no write permission. |
| `kernel` | ✗ | `run scripts/build-kernel.sh, or set VLO_KERNEL_WASM` | The wasm is missing beside `src/` or `dist/`; build it with `scripts/build-kernel.sh` or point `VLO_KERNEL_WASM` at one. |
| `kernel` | ⚠ | `over the 1024 KiB budget; build with --release` | A debug build was committed. |
| `kernel` | ✗ | `this SDK speaks protocol 1; rebuild the kernel` | Protocol mismatch between the wasm and the SDK. |
| `schemas` | ⚠ | `these register on the next host boot` | No host has booted this build yet; not an error. |
| `queue:<name>` | ✗ | `give the queue a url, or export defineWorker({ … }, { queues: ["<name>"] })` | A push queue with no URL and no in-process worker can never be served. |
| `queue:<name>` | ✗ | `queue url must be absolute` | The URL did not parse. |
| `queue:<name>` | ✗ | `the worker host is up but not healthy` | `/healthz` on the queue's origin answered non-2xx. |
| `queue:<name>` | ✗ | `start the worker host, or fix the queue url` | `/healthz` was unreachable within 3 s. |
| `queue:<name>` | ⚠ | `set \`secret\` on the queue; unsigned pushes are rejected by the worker`| The dispatcher refuses to push unsigned; add the shared secret. |
|`roles`| ⚠ |`a manual dispatcher only advances on POST /v1/timers/tick; set \`deploy.cron\``| An orchestrator in`manual\` mode with no cron declared will never move the outbox. |

Details worth knowing: `journal` reports `<dialect> · commit round trip <n> ms`; `kernel`
reports `protocol <n> · <size> KiB`; `schemas` reports `<registered>/<wanted> registered ·
missing <names>`; a pull queue reports `pull · served by pollers`; with no queues configured
the single check `queues` reports `none configured · in-process only`.

# Limits

Hard caps, defaults you can raise, and what the current runtime cannot do. Every number
below is a constant in the source; the file is named so you can check it.

## Payload and state caps

| Limit | Value | Where | Behaviour at the limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inline payload | 256 KiB (262 144 bytes) | `INLINE_LIMIT_BYTES` in `crates/types/src/lib.rs` and `src/kernel/protocol.ts` | `validate_event` rejects a larger inline `payload` with `payload_too_large`. The host offloads oversized text to the blob store and sends `payload_ref` instead. |
| Inline user state | 256 KiB | same constant | The kernel sets `state_inline: false`; the host writes `run_state.state_ref` and the bytes go to the blob store. Folding then reads the blob on every event, so keep state small or `continue_as_new`. |
| Inline run output | 256 KiB | same constant | Offloaded to `runs.output_ref`; `GET /v1/runs/{id}` reads it back. |
| Blob reference | `blob://sha256/<64 lowercase hex>` | `src/blob/ref.ts` | Anything else is rejected. |
| `random` | exactly 32 lowercase hex chars | `crates/kernel/src/validate.rs` | `invalid_event` otherwise. |
| Child run id | `run_` + 26 hex | `crates/kernel/src/ids.rs` | Derived from `sha256("<run_id>:<step_id>")`. |

Numbers in hashed structures (`Usage`, `RetryPolicy`, `KernelState`) are integers. Money is
`cost_micro_usd`; there are no floats on the wire where a hash is taken.

## Size budgets (CI gate)

`sdk/ts/sdk/scripts/size-gate.mjs` fails the build when any budget is exceeded, or when code
that belongs to the CLI (argument parsing, doctor checks, deploy templates) appears in a chunk
the runtime imports:

| Artifact | Budget | Today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wasm/vlo_kernel_bg.wasm` | 1 MiB (1 048 576 bytes); also enforced by `scripts/build-kernel.sh` and warned on by `vlo doctor` | 297 573 bytes (298 KB), built with `opt-level = "z"`, fat LTO, `panic = "abort"`, `strip`, `wasm-opt` off |
| Runtime JS: every `dist/*.js` chunk reachable from `index.js` and `host.js` (what `@oona/vlo` and `@oona/vlo/host` load) | 256 KB (262 144 bytes) | ~207 KB |
| CLI JS: `cli.js` and the chunks only it reaches | 96 KB (98 304 bytes) | ~54 KB |

The CI gate on the kernel is semantic, not byte-identical: the committed wasm and a
freshly built one must both pass every golden fixture (see [kernel protocol](kernel-protocol.md)).

## Known weak spots

These are measured, not theoretical. The setup behind the numbers is in
[performance.md](./performance.md#setup).

| Weak spot | What was measured | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Database round trips per step** | One step makes about 15 round trips to the database, so step time is roughly 15 times the round trip. With a 23 ms round trip, a step took 336 ms. | Run the host in the same region as its journal. |
| **Very wide fan-out in one run** | 1,000 tasks inside a single run finished at 45 per second, against 975 per second across separate runs. Per-task cost grows with the width of the run. | Fan out wide work as child runs with `fanOutRuns`, each with its own journal. |
| **Throughput is bounded by the database** | By design: low thousands of tasks per second on Postgres. Not load-tested on server hardware. | Add a broker as a delivery transport if you need more; the journal still records everything. |
| **Reducer purity is not enforced** | A TypeScript reducer could read the clock or call the network, and no lint catches it. | Keep reducers pure. A mistake surfaces as `nondeterminism_detected` when a run is rebuilt. |

## Dispatcher, lease and retry defaults

| Knob | Default | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dispatcher tick | 500 ms (`loop` mode only) | `DispatcherOptions.tickMs` |
| Claim batch | 50 rows per stage per pass | `DispatcherOptions.batch` |
| Claim hold | 30 s | `DispatcherOptions.claimHoldMs` |
| Refused-push backoff | 1 s × 2^attempts, capped at 60 s | `backoffBaseMs`, `maxBackoffMs` |
| Unroutable queue backoff | 60 s | `unroutableBackoffMs` |
| Drain time box | 25 s | `DEFAULT_DRAIN_MAX_MS`; `?max_ms=` on the tick route |
| Task lease | 60 s | `DEFAULT_LEASE_MS` (SDK), `DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_MS` (kernel); `activity({ leaseMs })` |
| Heartbeat interval | `max(1000, lease / 3)` ms | `toPushedTask` |
| Attempt timeout | none | `activity({ timeoutMs })` |
| Retry policy | 3 attempts, exponential, 1 s initial, 600 s max, factor 2, full jitter | `DEFAULT_RETRY` |
| Push request timeout | 5 s | `HttpPushTransport` |
| Callback request timeout | 10 s | `remoteReporter` |
| Push signature window | ±5 min | `src/host/worker/signature.ts` |
| Signed link TTL | 7 days | `DEFAULT_LINK_TTL_MS` |
| Poll long-wait | ≤ 25 s, ≤ 10 tasks, recheck 500 ms | `src/host/api/poll.ts` |
| Pull worker | 20 s wait, concurrency 4, ≤ 10 per poll, 1 s backoff after a failed poll | `runPullWorker` |
| SSE poll | 500 ms; keepalive every 15 s | `streamPollMs`, `KEEPALIVE_MS` |
| Run list | 50 via the route, 100 via `journal.query` | `indexRuns`, `DEFAULT_QUERY_LIMIT` |
| Shutdown grace | 5 s for in-process handlers | `SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS` |
| Default port | 4100, bound to `127.0.0.1` | `DEFAULT_PORT`, `listen()` |
| Agent loop | 50 iterations, 20 observations kept | `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS`, `DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIMIT` in `@oona/vlo/agent` |

A missed heartbeat window moves the attempt to `retrying` with `cause: heartbeat_lost`, or to
`failed` once the policy is spent. `schema_violation`, `user_cancel` and
`nondeterminism_detected` never retry, whatever the policy.

## SQLite is single-writer

The SQLite journal is one `node:sqlite` connection behind a promise mutex; every transaction
takes the file's write lock with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Consequences:

* Run **one host process per SQLite file**. A second process waits on the lock for
  `busy_timeout` (5 s) and then errors; two `SqliteJournal` instances in one process must
  never both be opened on the same file.
* Throughput is one transaction at a time. It is the right journal for a laptop, CI and a
  small self-host, not for fan-out in the thousands.
* Postgres has no such constraint: claims use `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and per-run advisory
  locks, so several orchestrators may tick the same journal at once.

## Runtime

* **Node ≥ 22.5** (`engines` in both packages), because the SQLite journal uses `node:sqlite`
  and the kernel is instantiated with `WebAssembly` from bytes read off disk.
* `zod` ^4 is a peer dependency of both packages; `@google-cloud/storage` ^7 is optional and
  only needed for `gcs://`.
* The workflow bundle digest is currently `contentHash({ name, v: 1 })`: a run pins the
  workflow name, not its code. Changing a reducer's behaviour under a live run is caught by
  the re-fold check, not prevented.

## Not available on edge runtimes yet

Vlo is built to run at the edge, and it does not run there yet. The host runs on Node
today. The kernel already compiles to `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with no
imports, which is what an edge host needs, but the surrounding pieces are Node-only:

* **Cloudflare Workers / Durable Objects** as a host and journal are deferred. There is no
  Durable Object journal adapter, no `wrangler.toml` emitter, and the journal is opened with
  `pg` or `node:sqlite`.
* **No cross-run index** outside the `runs` table: listing and searching runs is a SQL query
  against Postgres or SQLite.
* **No console.** The inbox is `GET /v1/runs?status=awaiting_signal`; the timeline is the
  events route.
* **No S3 or Vercel Blob adapter**: blob stores are `file://` and `gcs://`.
* **No `vlo.toml`, no native (non-Node) host**: `crates/traits` sketches the adapter traits a
  Rust host would implement, and nothing implements them.
* `vlo deploy` renders templates for two targets, `cloud-run` and `vercel`, and prints the
  commands with `--apply`; it never runs them.
